# Getting Started with Frontdesk

Frontdesk is an AI-powered receptionist platform that answers your business phone calls, sends text messages, collects customer information, schedules appointments, and more -- all without you needing to pick up the phone.

## What Frontdesk Does

When a customer calls your business number, your AI receptionist answers using a greeting you define. It can:

- Answer questions about your business using knowledge you provide
- Transfer calls to specific people or departments based on rules you set
- Send text messages to callers during or after the call (such as links, menus, or confirmations)
- Collect information from callers using intake forms
- Schedule appointments by connecting to your calendar
- Log every call, text, and voicemail for you to review later

You also get an Outbound Suite for running outbound calling campaigns, and a website chatbot you can embed on your site.

## How It Works

Frontdesk gives your AI receptionist its own phone number. You forward your business line to that number, or use it directly. When a call comes in, the AI handles the conversation based on the configuration you set up in your dashboard. No coding required.

Everything your receptionist does is logged. You can review call transcripts, listen to recordings, read text message histories, and see voicemails -- all from one place.

## Signing Up

When you create your Frontdesk account, you go through a short setup flow:

1. Enter your email -- Provide your email address and create your login credentials.
2. Business details -- Tell us your business name and type so the AI can represent you accurately.
3. Quick setup questions -- Answer a few questions about how you want calls handled.
4. Receptionist details -- Name your AI receptionist and provide basic configuration.
5. Email verification -- Confirm your email with a one-time code.

After signing up, you land in your dashboard where you can finish configuring your receptionist, test it, and go live.

## What to Expect After Signing Up

Once your account is created, you will have access to:

- Your AI receptionist with a provisioned phone number
- A dashboard showing calls answered, texts sent, and estimated business impact
- A setup checklist (the Configure tab) walking you through each configuration step
- A Playground to test your receptionist by voice or phone before going live
- Call, text, and voicemail logs so you never miss a customer interaction

Your next steps should be:

1. Complete the setup checklist under Receptionist > Configure
2. Test your receptionist in the Playground
3. Set up notifications so you are alerted about calls and messages
4. Forward your business phone number to your Frontdesk number, or share the number directly

## Inbound and Outbound Suites

Your Frontdesk account is organized into two suites visible on the Dashboard:

- Inbound Suite -- Your AI Receptionist, an AI Website Embeddable (chatbot), and an AI Texting Agent. This handles all incoming customer communication.
- Outbound Suite -- For outbound calling campaigns where the AI initiates calls to contacts on your behalf.

You can subscribe to either or both suites. If you do not have an active subscription, the Dashboard shows options to Subscribe Now or Create Demo Account for each suite.

## Key Concepts

- Agent -- Your AI receptionist instance. Each agent has its own phone number, configuration, and logs. You can have multiple agents under one account.
- Workflows -- Rules that tell your receptionist what to do during a call (transfer calls, send texts, collect information).
- Knowledge Base -- The business information your receptionist draws on to answer caller questions.
- Provisioned Number -- The phone number assigned to your AI receptionist.

## Getting Help

A dedicated Customer Success Manager is assigned to your account. You can find their name, email, and a link to book a call with them directly on the Dashboard page. You can also reach support through Get Live Help in the sidebar.

## Next Steps

- Your Dashboard -- Learn how to navigate the main dashboard
- Setting Up Your AI Receptionist -- Walk through the configuration checklist
- Testing Your Receptionist -- Make your first test call

# Your Dashboard

The dashboard is your command center for monitoring and managing your AI receptionist. It gives you a quick overview of activity, access to your AI agents, and a way to reach your Customer Success Manager.

## Getting to the Dashboard

When you log in, you land on the Dashboard page. You can always return to it by clicking Dashboard at the top of the sidebar. The page header reads "Your AI Frontdesk at a glance."

## Key Metrics

At the top of the dashboard, three stat cards show your activity over the last 7 days:

- Calls Answered (Last 7 days) -- Total calls your AI receptionist handled, with a daily trend chart
- Texts Sent (Last 7 days) -- Total text messages sent by your receptionist, with a daily trend chart
- Revenue Impact (Last 7 days) -- Estimated revenue based on an average of $25 per call answered, with a daily trend chart

Each card includes a small area chart showing the daily breakdown for the past week.

## My AI Agents

Below the metrics, the My AI Agents section displays your agents in two columns:

### Inbound Suite

Your inbound agents appear here. Each agent card is expandable and shows the sub-agents available:

- AI Receptionist -- Your phone-answering AI
- AI Website Embeddable -- A chatbot you can embed on your website
- AI Texting Agent -- Handles text message conversations

If you have an active subscription, you can click Add More Receptionist to create additional agents.

If you do not have a subscription yet, you will see a prompt to Subscribe Now or Create Demo Account.

### Outbound Suite

Your outbound campaign agents appear here. Each agent card expands to show Outbound Campaigns.

If you do not have an outbound subscription, you will see options to Subscribe Now or Create Demo Account.

## Recent Activity

The Recent Activity section shows your three most recent calls and texts from the past 7 days. Each entry includes:

- Whether it was a phone call or text message
- The caller's name or phone number
- A brief summary or content preview
- The date and time (shown in your agent's configured timezone)

Click View All to go to the full call logs.

## Customer Success Manager

On the right side of the dashboard, a card shows your assigned Customer Success Manager with:

- Their name, title, and photo
- A link to book a call via Calendly
- A Request an Integration button that opens a form where you can describe integrations you need with your existing tools

## Sidebar Navigation

The sidebar organizes all features into groups:

Top-level items:

- Dashboard -- The overview page described here
- Ask Frontdesk -- AI-powered assistant for configuring your receptionist

AI Workers:

- Receptionist -- Configure your AI receptionist (greeting, workflows, knowledge base, and more)
- Chatbot -- Website chatbot embeddable widget
- Web Forms -- Manage web forms

Customer Hub:

- Call Log Inbox -- Unified inbox for all call activity
- CRM (Customers) -- Contact and lead management
- Outbound -- Automated outbound campaigns
- Calendar -- Calendar and appointment management
- Tickets -- Support ticket tracking
- Notify Me -- Notification preferences
- Analytics -- Usage statistics and charts

Bottom items:

- Settings -- Account and agent settings
- Get Live Help -- Contact support

## Agent Home Page

When you are viewing a specific agent (rather than the organization-level dashboard), the Overview page shows a welcome message: "Welcome back, [Agent Name]." It displays your receptionist's provisioned phone number and summary cards:

- Estimated Time Saved -- Based on 7 minutes saved per call answered
- Estimated Revenue -- Based on $30 estimated per text sent
- Calls -- Total call count with a View Details button
- Voicemails -- Total voicemail count with a View Details button
- Texts -- Total text message count with a View Details button
- Edit Receptionist -- Quick link to the configuration page
- Notifications -- Quick link to notification settings
- Free Month -- Referral program (invite a friend, both get a free month)

Each card has a View Details button that navigates to the relevant section.

## Next Steps

- Setting Up Your AI Receptionist -- Configure your receptionist step by step
- Testing Your Receptionist -- Make your first test call

# Setting Up Your AI Receptionist

The Receptionist page is where you configure everything about how your AI answers calls. It is organized into two tabs: Configure and Notifications. The Configure tab shows a completion tracker ("Completed X/Y") so you can see your setup progress at a glance.

## Accessing the Setup Page

Click Receptionist in the sidebar under AI Workers. The Configure tab opens by default.

## How the Configure Page Is Organized

Settings are grouped into collapsible sections. Click any item to expand it and make changes. Each item has a badge indicating its importance:

- Required -- Must be completed for basic functionality
- Recommended -- Strongly suggested for a good caller experience
- Optional -- Nice to have but not essential
- Advanced -- For power users and developer integrations
- Enabled -- Already active on your account

The completion tracker at the top of the Configure tab counts how many items you have filled in out of the total available. It excludes Advanced Settings from the count.

## Basic Settings

These are the foundational settings for your receptionist.

### Greeting Phrase

The opening line your receptionist uses when answering the phone. For example: "Thank you for calling Acme Plumbing, how can I help you today?"

### Custom Commands

Customize the prompts that guide your AI receptionist's behavior. You can set separate prompts for voice calls and text conversations.

### Business Information

Provide the information your receptionist needs to answer caller questions. You can add content in three ways:

- Plain text
- A website URL (the AI will read the page)
- Upload documents

### Common Questions

Add frequently asked questions and their answers. Your receptionist references these when callers ask similar questions.

### Languages

Make your receptionist multilingual. Select which languages it should support.

### Choose Voice

Select the voice your AI receptionist uses when speaking to callers. Browse featured voices and pick one that fits your brand.

## In-Call Actions

These settings control what your receptionist can do during a live call.

### Transfer Call

Set up rules for when and how your receptionist should transfer calls to a real person. You define the scenario (e.g., "caller asks for the manager") and the phone number to transfer to. You can listen to a sample audio clip demonstrating how the AI handles call transfers.

### Send Text Message

Your receptionist can text the caller during the call -- useful for sending links, menus, appointment confirmations, or any information that is easier to read than hear. A sample audio clip is available to hear how this works.

### Collect Information (Intake Form)

Set up forms that your receptionist fills out by asking the caller questions during the call. For example, collecting a name, email, and reason for calling. Responses are stored and available in your intake form logs. A sample audio clip demonstrates this feature.

### Schedule an Appointment

Connect your calendar so your receptionist can book appointments in real time during the call. This integrates with your calendar provider for live availability checking.

## After-Call Actions

These settings control what happens after a call ends.

### Send a Text to Caller

If a caller hangs up on your receptionist, automatically send them a follow-up text message to re-engage them. Your texting AI continues the conversation over text.

### Smart Call Analysis

AI-powered summaries and outcomes are generated automatically after each call. This is enabled by default.

## Developer Automations

For technical users who want to connect Frontdesk to other systems.

### API Integration

Your receptionist can make real-time API requests during a phone call -- retrieving or submitting information to your systems while the caller is on the line.

### Zapier Integration

Connect your AI receptionist to 6,000+ apps through Zapier. Automate workflows that trigger after each call.

### Custom Webhook

Send call data to your own webhook endpoint after each call for custom processing.

## Advanced Settings

Additional controls including extension digits, call recording preferences, and other fine-tuning options.

## Notifications Tab

Switch to the Notifications tab to configure how you are notified about calls, texts, and voicemails. This tab is labeled as "Recommended" to encourage you to set it up.

## Completion Tracking

The Configure tab header shows Completed X/Y where:

- X = the number of items you have configured
- Y = the total number of configurable items (excluding Advanced Settings)

Items count as completed when they have content. For example:

- Greeting Phrase is complete when you have set a greeting
- Business Information is complete when you have added at least one knowledge source
- Transfer Call is complete when you have at least one call transfer workflow
- Send Text Message is complete when you have at least one texting workflow
- Languages is complete when you have selected a voice and languages

Work through each section until your completion count is maximized. You can always come back and adjust settings later.

## Next Steps

- Testing Your Receptionist -- Make a test call to hear your configuration in action

# Testing Your Receptionist

Once you have configured your AI receptionist, use the Playground to test it. The Playground lets you hear exactly how your receptionist will sound to callers, verify that workflows are working, and share a demo with others.

## Accessing the Playground

The Playground is available from within the Receptionist page. The page header reads Playground and prompts you with "How would you like to connect?" followed by "Choose your preferred way to test."

## Testing Options

The Playground presents up to three options depending on your account type and subscription:

### Join Audio

Click the Join Audio card to start a voice call directly in your browser. This opens an in-browser audio session where you can speak to your receptionist as if you were a real caller.

What to know:

- The call happens entirely in your browser -- no phone needed
- Text SMS sending and call transferring do not work during browser-based test calls
- Your account must have available voice credits to make a test call

After selecting Join Audio, the heading changes to Join Audio and the call interface appears. Click the close button (X) to end the session and return to the card selection screen.

### Receive Call

Click the Receive Call card to have your AI receptionist call your testing number. This is the most realistic way to test because the call comes through on an actual phone.

What to know:

- The call goes to the testing number configured on your account
- Testing calls have a maximum duration of 15 minutes
- If you do not have the testing phone with you, click the button labeled "I don't have [your number] with me" to open the Change Testing Number form and update it
- Your account must have available voice credits

After selecting Receive Call, the screen shows "Calling [your testing number]..." with a Cancel button to stop the call.

### Share Demo

Click the Share Demo card to copy a shareable link to your clipboard. Anyone with this link can interact with your receptionist demo.

What to know:

- The shareable URL is copied automatically when you click the card
- A confirmation appears: "URL copied to clipboard!"
- You can click Copy Link Again to copy it a second time
- This option is available to account owners

## Credit Requirements

Before any test call (Join Audio or Receive Call), the system checks whether your account has sufficient voice credits. If you do not have enough credits, an Insufficient Credits modal appears with options to:

- Start a subscription trial
- Manage your credits

The insufficient credits modal shows different options based on your account type. Paid users see a Manage Credits button, demo users see Start Subscription, and reseller clients without an active subscription see a Close button with a message to contact their administrator.

## Changing Your Testing Number

If you need to receive test calls on a different phone:

1. Select Receive Call in the Playground
2. Click the button that says "I don't have [your number] with me"
3. The Change Testing Number modal opens
4. Enter your new phone number
5. Submit the form

Your testing number updates immediately and future test calls will go to the new number.

## Verification

The Playground uses reCAPTCHA verification to prevent abuse. This runs automatically in the background when the page loads -- you do not need to take any action.

## Tips for Effective Testing

- Test after each configuration change. Made a new texting workflow? Test it. Changed the greeting? Test it. This way you catch issues early.
- Use Receive Call for the full experience. Browser-based calls (Join Audio) do not support SMS or call transfers. To test those features, use Receive Call.
- Share your demo link for feedback. Before going live, send the share link to a colleague or friend and ask them to call in. Fresh ears catch things you might miss.
- Check your call logs after testing. Every test call appears in your Call Log Inbox with a full transcript and summary. Review these to see exactly what the AI said and how it handled the conversation.

# Greeting Phrase

The greeting phrase is the first thing callers hear when your AI receptionist answers the phone. A well-crafted greeting sets the tone for the entire conversation and lets callers know they have reached your business.

## Where to find it

Your greeting phrase is located on the Overview page of your receptionist dashboard, under the Greeting Phrases section.

## Editing your greeting phrase

1. In the Greeting Phrases section, click the Edit button in the top-right corner.
2. Type your greeting in the English text field.
3. Click Update to save your changes, or click Cancel to discard them.

## Best practices for greeting phrases

Keep your greeting short and direct. A good example:
"Welcome to [your business name], how may I help you?"

If your greeting is too long (more than 15 words), the dashboard will display a warning. Research shows that 75% of callers hang up when the greeting is too long because they assume they have reached a voicemail.

## Multi-language greetings

If you have enabled additional languages for your receptionist, separate greeting fields will appear for each language you have selected. Each language has its own text field labeled with the language name (for example, Spanish, French).

To set a greeting for another language:

1. Click Edit on the Greeting Phrases section.
2. Scroll down to the field for the desired language.
3. Enter your greeting in that language.
4. Click Update to save all greetings at once.

If you do not provide a custom greeting for an additional language, a default example greeting for that language will be used automatically. For instance, the default Spanish greeting is "Hola, en que puedo ayudarte?" and the default French greeting is "Bonjour, comment puis-je vous aider?"

## Tips

- Mention your business name so callers know they reached the right place.
- End with an open question like "How may I help you?" to prompt the caller to speak.
- Avoid including hours, addresses, or other details in the greeting -- save that for the knowledge base.

# Custom Commands (AI Prompt)

Custom commands let you control how your AI receptionist behaves during phone calls and text conversations. This is where you write instructions that shape the receptionist's personality, tone, and responses.

## Where to find it

Custom commands are located on the Overview page of your receptionist dashboard, in the Custom Commands section (also referred to as the AI Prompt).

## Voice and text prompts

Your receptionist can have separate instructions for voice calls and text messages.

- The Voice tab contains the prompt used during phone calls.
- The Text tab contains the prompt used for text/SMS conversations.

The Text tab is only visible to users with the texting chatbot feature enabled. If you don't see the Text tab, only the Voice tab will be available for configuring your AI prompt.

If you have not set a custom text prompt, the receptionist will fall back to using the voice prompt for text conversations as well. A note will appear saying "Using the default prompt. Click Edit to customize the text prompt."

## Editing your custom commands

1. Select the Voice or Text tab depending on which prompt you want to edit.
2. Click the Edit button below the current prompt.
3. Type your instructions in the text field.
4. Click Update Voice Prompt (or Update Text Prompt) to save, or click Cancel to discard.

## What to include in your custom commands

Custom commands are written in plain language. Think of them as instructions you would give to a real receptionist on their first day. Here are some ideas:

- Personality and tone: "Be friendly and professional. Keep responses concise."
- Business rules: "We do not offer refunds after 30 days."
- Call handling: "If someone asks for the manager, take their name and number and say someone will call them back."
- Appointment guidance: "When someone wants to book an appointment, ask for their name, phone number, and preferred date."
- Topics to avoid: "Do not discuss pricing for custom projects. Ask them to email us instead."
- Specific phrasing: "Always refer to our company as 'Smith & Associates,' never just 'Smith.'"

## Tips

- Be specific. Vague instructions lead to vague responses.
- Test your changes by calling your receptionist number after saving.
- You can update your custom commands as often as you like.
- If something is not working as expected, try rewording your instruction to be more direct.

# Knowledge Base

The knowledge base is where you provide your AI receptionist with information about your business. The more detailed and accurate this information is, the better your receptionist will be at answering caller questions.

## Where to find it

The knowledge base is located on the Overview page of your receptionist dashboard. There are two related sections:

- Knowledge Base -- for adding business information through text, website URLs, or document uploads.
- Questions and Answers (Q&A) -- for adding specific question-and-answer pairs.

## Adding knowledge base entries

You can add information to your knowledge base in three ways. Use the buttons at the top of the Knowledge Base section:

### Add text

1. Click Add Text.
2. In the Add Text Knowledge Base modal, type or paste your business information.
3. Click Add to save.

This is ideal for pasting general business information such as your services, policies, history, and mission statement. You can enter up to 100,000 characters per text entry.

### Add a website URL

1. Click Add Website URL (shown as Add URL on mobile).
2. Enter the URL of the webpage you want the AI to learn from.
3. The system will crawl the URL and display the pages it found. Select which pages to include (up to 3 URLs per entry).
4. Choose an auto-sync schedule if you want the content to stay up to date automatically. Options include:
   - No auto-update
   - Every 30 minutes
   - Hourly
   - Every 6 hours
   - Daily
   - Weekly
   - Every 10 days
   - Every 2 weeks

Note: Some sync frequencies may not be available depending on your plan.
5. Click OK to save.

For URL entries with auto-sync enabled, you can also click the Sync Now button on the knowledge base card to manually trigger an update at any time.

### Upload a document

1. Click Upload Document (shown as Add Document on mobile).
2. Select a file from your computer. Supported formats: PDF, DOCX, TXT. Maximum file size: 20 MB.
3. Optionally add transform instructions to tell the AI how to interpret the document.
4. Click Upload to confirm.

The AI will process the document and extract relevant information. Processing can take 3-5 minutes depending on the size of the document.

## Managing knowledge base entries

Each entry appears as a card showing a preview of its content, its type (text, link, or file), and its status.

### Entry statuses

- Active -- The entry is being used by your receptionist. An active/inactive toggle switch appears on each card.
- Inactive -- The entry is saved but not being used. Toggle the switch on the card to reactivate it.
- Processing -- The AI is still extracting information from your source. This typically takes 3-5 minutes. The page automatically checks for updates while entries are processing.
- Failed -- The AI could not extract data from the source. Try syncing again or delete the entry and add it again.

### Editing an entry

Click on any text-type card to open it for editing. URL and file entries open in a view-only modal where you can review the extracted content.

### Deleting an entry

Click the delete icon on any card, then confirm the deletion in the modal that appears.

### Searching entries

Use the search field at the top of the knowledge base section to search across all your entries by keyword. Matching text will be highlighted in the results.

## Token usage

Each knowledge base entry consumes tokens, which represent how much information the AI can process in a single conversation. A progress bar at the top of the section shows your total token usage relative to the limit. If you approach or exceed the token limit, a warning will appear and you will not be able to add new entries until you deactivate or delete existing ones.

Note: Tokens are not the same as characters. Approximately 4 characters consume 1 token.

## Questions and Answers (Q&A)

The Q&A section lets you provide precise answers to common caller questions.

### Adding Q&A pairs

1. In the Questions and Answers section, click Edit.
2. In the modal, enter your questions and answers using this format:

Question: Where are you located?
Answer: We are located at 132 Linkin Park, New York.

Question: How many other branches do you have?
Answer: We don't have any subsidiary branches.

3. Separate each Q&A pair with a blank line.
4. Click Save to apply your changes.

### Tips for Q&A

- Use the exact phrasing your callers tend to use. If customers usually ask "What time do you close?" use that wording rather than "What are your operating hours?"
- Keep answers concise and direct.
- You can add as many Q&A pairs as you need.

# Choosing a Voice

Your AI receptionist's voice is one of the first things callers notice. The Voice Library gives you access to a wide selection of pre-built voices, and you can also clone your own voice for a fully personalized experience.

## Where to find it

You can browse and select voices in two places:

- Overview page -- The Featured Voices section on your receptionist dashboard shows your currently selected voice and a curated set of featured options. Click Explore All Voices to open the full library.
- Voice Library page -- The dedicated Voice Library page (accessible from the sidebar) provides the complete browsing and filtering experience.

## Browsing the Voice Library

The Voice Library page is organized into three sections:

- Current Voice -- Shows the voice (or voices) currently assigned to your receptionist. If you have multiple languages enabled, you may see separate cards for your English voice and your multilingual voice.
- Featured Voices -- A curated selection of recommended voices.
- All Voices -- The full catalog of available voices, with search and filtering.

### Voice card details

Each voice is displayed as a card showing:

- Name -- The voice name and initials.
- Provider -- The underlying voice technology (e.g., Cartesia, ElevenLabs, Deepgram, OpenAI, Rime, Fish Audio).
- Language -- Whether the voice supports English, multilingual, or a specific language.
- Gender -- Male or female.
- Credits per minute -- How many credits the voice costs to use (typically 1 credit/min; some premium speech-to-speech models cost 2 credits/min).
- Description -- A short summary of the voice's characteristics.

### Previewing a voice

Click the play button on any voice card to hear a sample. While a sample is playing, other voice cards will be dimmed. Click pause to stop playback.

### Selecting a voice

To apply a voice to your receptionist, click the play button on the card you want. The voice will be applied automatically. The currently active voice shows a blue checkmark badge and an Active label.

## Searching and filtering

### Search

Use the Search voices... field above the All Voices section to find voices by name.

### Filters

Click the Filters button to open a filter popup where you can narrow results by:

- Provider -- Filter by voice technology provider.
- Language -- Filter by supported language (English, Multilingual, and others).
- Gender -- Filter by male or female voices.
- Accent -- Filter by accent (e.g., American, British, Australian).

Active filters appear as tags above the voice grid. Click the X on any tag to remove that filter, or click Clear all to reset all filters.

## Voice settings

For selected voices from supported providers (Cartesia, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Rime, Fish Audio), you can fine-tune voice settings. Hover over your active voice card and click the gear icon that appears.

Available settings vary by provider but may include:

- Voice model -- Choose between different model versions.
- Speed -- Adjust how fast the voice speaks.
- Emotion and emotion level -- Set the emotional tone (available for some providers).
- Accent, intonation, tone, and impression -- Fine-tune vocal characteristics (OpenAI voices).
- Temperature -- Control variation in speech output (Rime voices).

Click OK in the settings modal to apply your changes.

## Cloning a voice

You can create a custom voice clone from an audio recording. Switch to the Clone Voice tab at the top of the Voice Library page.

### How to clone a voice

1. Click the Clone Voice tab.
2. Enter a Voice Name and Description for your custom voice.
3. Choose a Voice Provider: Elevenlabs or Cartesia.
4. Provide an audio source by either:
   - Clicking Select File to upload an audio file (WAV or MP3, up to 10 MB).
   - Clicking Start Recording to record directly from your microphone. Click Stop Recording when finished.
5. Click Create Voice Clone.

Once created, your cloned voice will appear under Your Cloned Voices on the Clone Voice tab. You can select it just like any other voice in the library.

## Credits

Different voice providers consume credits at different rates. If you are unsure about credit costs, click the How Credits Work button in the top-right corner of the Voice Library page to view a breakdown.

## Tips

- Preview several voices before committing -- the right voice depends on your brand and audience.
- If you have multiple languages enabled, you can assign different voices for English calls and non-English calls.
- Cloned voices work best with clear, high-quality audio recordings.

# Language Settings

Your AI receptionist can handle calls in multiple languages. When you enable additional languages, callers will hear a language selection prompt at the start of the call and can choose the language they prefer.

## Where to find it

Language settings are located on the Overview page of your receptionist dashboard, in the Languages section.

## Viewing your current languages

The Languages section shows the languages currently enabled for your receptionist as a comma-separated list (for example, "English, Spanish, French").

## Changing your languages

1. In the Languages section, click Edit.
2. In the Select Languages modal, use the Select Languages (BETA) dropdown to add or remove languages.
3. Click Save to apply your changes.

English is included by default. You can add as many additional languages as your plan supports.

### Available languages

Frontdesk AI supports a wide range of languages, including but not limited to:

- Cartesia-supported voices: English, German, Portuguese, Mandarin, Japanese, French, Spanish, Hindi, Italian, Korean, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Swedish, Turkish
- Additional languages: Arabic, Armenian, Bulgarian, Catalan, Czech, Danish, Estonian, Finnish, Flemish, Greek, Haitian Creole, Hungarian, Indonesian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Malay, Norwegian, Romanian, Slovak, Swiss German, Thai, Ukrainian, Vietnamese

The list of available languages is loaded from a configuration file and currently includes over 40 languages. The full list is displayed in the language selector when configuring your receptionist.

## How multilingual calls work

When more than one language is selected, callers hear a language selection prompt at the beginning of each call. The receptionist then conducts the rest of the conversation in the chosen language.

### Important note about caller experience

The dashboard includes this advisory: "Our data indicates that 90% of callers hang up when they hear the initial language selection prompt." Frontdesk AI recommends against enabling multiple languages unless a significant portion of your callers speak different languages.

## Multilingual voice selection

When you enable non-English languages, you can assign a separate voice for non-English calls. This is managed in the Voice Library.

- Your English voice is used for English calls.
- Your multilingual voice is used for calls in all other selected languages.

Some voice providers do not support all languages. If you select a language that is not supported by your chosen Cartesia voice, the system will automatically use Deepgram's Helio voice for those languages. You can also choose your own Deepgram or ElevenLabs voice as an alternative.

## Multi-language greetings

When additional languages are enabled, separate greeting fields appear in the Greeting Phrase settings for each language. This lets you write a natural greeting in each language rather than relying on a translation of your English greeting.

## Plan requirements

Multilingual support is an advanced capability. If your current plan does not include it, you will see a message with a link to upgrade: "You can't select multiple languages in this tier. Click here to upgrade."

## Tips

- Only enable multiple languages if your callers genuinely need them -- the language selection prompt adds friction to the call experience.
- Set custom greetings for each language so callers hear a natural-sounding welcome.
- Test your receptionist in each enabled language to make sure the voice and responses sound correct.

# Call Transfer Workflows

Call transfer workflows tell your AI receptionist when and where to forward calls to a live person. You define scenario-based rules -- for example, "transfer to billing when the caller asks about a refund" -- and the AI automatically routes the call to the right number.

## Where to find it

Call transfer workflows are located on the Overview page of your receptionist dashboard, under the Call Transferring Workflow section.

## Adding a call transfer workflow

1. In the Call Transferring Workflow section, click Add.
2. The Add Call Transferring Workflow modal opens with a new scenario card.
3. Fill in the required fields described below, then click Save to create the workflow.

### Scenario Description

Describe when the AI should transfer the call. Be specific so the AI knows exactly when to trigger it.

Example: "Transfer the caller to the billing department. Execute whenever caller asks for a refund or receipt."

### Phone Number

Enter the phone number you want the AI to forward calls to when this scenario is triggered.

You can also enter an optional Extension digit. This is useful when transferring to an IVR system (for example, extension 302). When you set an extension, the transfer type automatically switches to Hot Transfer.

### Voice Response

Enter what the AI should say to the caller right before the transfer begins. If you leave this blank, the default is "Please hold while I transfer your call."

Example: "Sounds good, I am transferring you to the billing department right now. Please hold."

## Advanced settings

Expand the Advanced Settings section inside a scenario card to configure the transfer type and additional options.

### Call Transfer Type

- Cold Transfer -- A standard call transfer. The call is forwarded using the caller's number. Cold transfer is not available when an extension digit is set.
- Hot Transfer -- An advanced call transfer. The call is forwarded using the AI receptionist's number. Hot transfer supports extension digits, whisper handoff messages, backup numbers, blast call numbers, and custom ringing tones.

### Continue AI After Failed Call Transfer

Available with Hot Transfer only. When toggled on, if the transfer fails or the recipient does not answer, the AI receptionist resumes the conversation with the caller instead of ending the call.

You can customize what the AI says when returning to the caller (for example, "Call Transfer was not successful, how can I assist you more?").

### Whisper Handoff Type

Available with Hot Transfer only. A whisper message is played to the person receiving the transferred call so they have context before speaking. Choose from:

- Auto-generate (AI summarizes conversation) -- The AI creates a summary of the conversation automatically.
- Custom AI Prompt (instruct the AI what to say) -- You instruct the AI what to say (for example, "Tell them the caller is asking about a refund").
- None -- No whisper message is played.

### Backup Numbers

Available with Hot Transfer only. If the primary transfer number does not connect, the AI dials backup numbers one by one in order. Click Add Another Backup Number to add more.

### Blast Call Numbers

Available with Hot Transfer only. Blast call numbers are dialed in parallel along with the main transfer number. All numbers ring simultaneously, and the first person to answer is connected. The other calls are automatically canceled. Click Add Another Blast Call Number to add more.

### Call Transfer Ringing Tone

Available with Hot Transfer only. Toggle this on to play a custom ringing tone for the caller while they wait for the transfer to connect. Upload an audio file (.mp3 or .wav, max 1 MB) using the Upload tone button.

## Managing existing workflows

Each scenario appears as a numbered card (for example, Scenario 1, Scenario 2).

- On/Off toggle -- Enable or disable a scenario without deleting it.
- Edit -- Open the scenario in edit mode to change any field.
- Delete -- Remove the scenario permanently. You will be asked to confirm before deletion.
- Duplicate -- Create a copy of an existing scenario, which you can then customize.
- Availability -- Set operating hours for the scenario. You can choose business hours, weekends, or a custom schedule. When the scenario is scheduled, a blue Scheduled tag appears on the card.

## Tips

- You can create up to 100 scenarios across all workflow types.
- Use clear, specific descriptions so the AI can accurately identify when to trigger each transfer.
- If you have a team, consider using blast call numbers so the first available person picks up.
- Test your call transfer workflows by calling your AI receptionist number and triggering the scenario.

# Text Message Workflows

Text message workflows let your AI receptionist automatically send an SMS to a caller during a phone call. You define the scenario that triggers the text and the exact message to send -- for example, "Send the caller a link to the menu whenever they ask about prices."

## Where to find it

Text message workflows are located on the Overview page of your receptionist dashboard, under the Texting Workflow section.

## Adding a text message workflow

1. In the Texting Workflow section, click Add.
2. The Add Texting Workflow modal opens with a new scenario card.
3. Fill in the fields described below, then click Save.

### Enable Short URLs

Toggle this on to automatically shorten any URLs in your text message. Shortened URLs let you track click analytics in the Analytics section of your dashboard. This is enabled by default.

### Scenario Description

Describe the situation in which the AI should send the text. The AI is smart enough to detect when the scenario applies.

Example: "Send the caller a copy of the menu. Execute whenever caller asks for menu or prices."

### Text Message

Enter the exact text you want to send. You can include URLs, promotional info, or anything the caller needs. The maximum length is 1,000 characters.

Example: "Here is our menu: www.restaurant.com/menu"

## Managing existing workflows

Each scenario appears as a numbered card (for example, Scenario 1, Scenario 2).

- On/Off toggle -- Enable or disable a scenario without deleting it.
- Edit -- Open the scenario to modify any field.
- Delete -- Remove the scenario permanently. You will be asked to confirm.
- Duplicate -- Create a copy of an existing scenario to customize.
- Availability -- Set operating hours for the scenario. When scheduled, a blue Scheduled tag appears on the card.

## Tips

- Use short URLs for any links so you can track how many callers click them.
- Keep text messages concise -- callers are more likely to read short messages.
- Use the "Ask before sending" option for sensitive or promotional content so callers opt in.
- You can create multiple text message scenarios for different situations (directions, menus, appointment links, and so on).

# Intake Forms

Intake forms let your AI receptionist collect structured information from callers by asking a series of questions during the call. The answers are captured and saved as tickets in your dashboard, making it easy to follow up.

## Where to find it

Intake forms are located on the Overview page of your receptionist dashboard, under the Intake Form (Phone Workflows) section.

## How intake forms work

Each intake form is a scenario with a trigger condition and a list of questions. When the trigger condition is met, the AI asks each question in order, collects the caller's answers, and submits the results as a ticket.

There are two types of scenarios:

- Beginning of Call -- Questions are asked at the start of every call, before the caller states their reason for calling. Only one "Beginning of Call" scenario can exist.
- Custom Scenario -- Questions are asked when a specific situation occurs during the call. You can create multiple custom scenarios.

## Adding an intake form scenario

1. In the Intake Form (Phone Workflows) section, click Add.
2. The Add New Scenerio modal opens.
3. Fill in the fields described below, then click Save.

### Title

Give your intake form a descriptive title. This title is used to group the tickets generated by this workflow (for example, "New Customer Intake" or "Service Request").

### Scenario Description

Choose when the questions should be asked:

- Beginning of Call -- Select this to ask questions at the start of every call. This option is disabled if a "Beginning of Call" scenario already exists.
- Define a custom scenario -- Select this and then describe the trigger condition in the text field that appears. Example: "Ask the new user some qualifying questions. Execute this anytime the user mentions they are a new customer."

### Questions

Add the questions you want the AI to ask. Each question is a separate field. You need at least one question per scenario.

- Click Add Question to add more questions.
- Drag and drop questions to reorder them.
- Click the minus icon next to a question to remove it.

Example questions: "What is your first and last name?", "What is your email address?", "What service are you interested in?"

### What should the AI do next?

Optionally, provide instructions for the AI to follow after completing the intake. This field appears for both "Beginning of Call" and custom scenarios.

Example: "Thank the caller for the information and ask if they would like to be transferred to customer support for assistance."

## Managing existing scenarios

Each scenario appears as a card. "Beginning of Call" scenarios are labeled as such; custom scenarios are numbered (for example, Custom Scenario 2).

- On/Off toggle -- Enable or disable a custom scenario without deleting it. The "Beginning of Call" scenario cannot be toggled off individually.
- Edit -- Open the scenario to change the title, description, questions, or post-execution instructions.
- Delete -- Remove the scenario. When deleting, you will be asked whether to also delete all tickets associated with this scenario.
- Duplicate -- Create a copy of a custom scenario to modify. The "Beginning of Call" scenario cannot be duplicated.
- Availability -- Set operating hours for a custom scenario. When scheduled, a blue Scheduled tag appears on the card.

### Deleting individual questions

You can delete a single question from a scenario by clicking the delete button next to it in the info view. If you delete the last question in a scenario, you will be prompted to delete the entire scenario.

## Tips

- Use the "Beginning of Call" scenario to capture essential details like name and phone number before the conversation begins.
- Keep questions short and clear so callers can answer quickly.
- Use the post-execution prompt to guide the AI toward the next step, such as transferring the call or sending a follow-up text.
- Review submitted tickets regularly in the Tickets section of your dashboard.

# Post-Call Text Messages

Post-call text messages let you automatically send an SMS to callers after the call ends. You can use them for follow-ups, feedback requests, or sharing additional information based on what happened during the call.

## Where to find it

Post-call text messages are located on the Overview page of your receptionist dashboard, under the Post Call Text Messages section.

## Adding a post-call message

1. In the Post Call Text Messages section, click Add.
2. The Add New Scenario modal opens.
3. Fill in the fields described below, then click Save.

### Trigger Type

Select when the text message should be sent. Choose from:

- After Every Call -- The message is sent after every call, regardless of what happened. Only one "After Every Call" scenario can exist.
- If the duration is less than -- The message is sent only if the call was shorter than a specified number of seconds. Enter the duration threshold in the field that appears (for example, 10 seconds). This is useful for following up with callers who may have hung up early. Only one "Duration Check" scenario can exist.
- Custom Scenario -- The message is sent when a condition you describe is met. Enter a description of the scenario in the text field that appears. Example: "If caller mentioned calling back." You can create multiple custom scenarios.

### Text Message

Enter the message to send. The maximum length is 500 characters. The placeholder text changes based on your selected trigger type to give you relevant examples.

## Managing existing scenarios

Each scenario appears as a numbered card (for example, Scenario 1, Scenario 2).

- Edit -- Open the scenario to change the trigger type or message.
- Delete -- Remove the scenario permanently. You will be asked to confirm.

You can click Add Another Scenario to add more scenarios. You can have one "After Every Call" trigger, one "Duration Check" trigger, and up to 10 total scenarios.

## Tips

- Use the "After Every Call" trigger for universal follow-ups like feedback forms or thank-you messages.
- Use "Duration Check" to reach out to callers who hung up quickly -- they may need help but did not get it.
- Keep messages concise and include a clear call-to-action (for example, a link to a feedback form or your website).

Control whether your AI receptionist uses CRM data (such as caller name and profile details) to personalize conversations. When turned off, the AI will not reference any CRM-based caller information.

When the AI has trouble understanding voice input, it can ask the caller to send the information via text message instead. This helps ensure accurate data collection even when voice recognition is challenging.

Click SMS Fallback for Voice Recognition to toggle it on or off. The current status is shown as a badge (On or Off).

## Auto Hangup after interaction ends

When enabled, the AI automatically ends the call when the interaction is clearly over. This helps avoid unnecessary call duration and reduces costs.

Click Auto Hangup after interaction ends to toggle it on or off. The current status is shown as a badge (On or Off).

## Auto Hangup after silence

Automatically end the call when the caller is silent for a specified duration. The value is displayed in minutes (up to 3 minutes).

Click Auto Hangup after silence to adjust the silence timeout.

## Idle Messages

Configure messages that your AI receptionist says when the caller has not responded for a period of time. This can prompt the caller to continue the conversation or let them know the AI is still on the line.

Click Idle Messages to configure.

## Time Control

Define specific time windows during which calls are automatically transferred to another number instead of being handled by the AI. This is useful for routing calls to a live person during business hours.

Click Time Control to open the Time Controls modal. Each rule has a Start Time, End Time, and Phone Number to transfer to.

Click Pronunciation Guides to open the configuration table. Each entry has a Word and its corresponding Pronunciation.

Set a maximum usage limit (in minutes) for your AI receptionist. When your usage reaches 50%, 75%, or 100% of the limit, you receive an email notification. This helps you stay on top of your billing.

Click Max Usage Limit to open the Set Maximum Usage Limit modal. The current status is shown as a badge (Enabled or Disabled).

Set the maximum call duration (in minutes) before the AI automatically hangs up. The current value is displayed next to the setting.

Click Maximum Call Duration to adjust the limit.

## Blocked Numbers

Maintain a list of phone numbers that are blocked from calling your receptionist. Blocked numbers will not be answered by the AI.

Click Blocked Numbers to view and manage the list.

Configure phrases that, when detected, automatically identify and block spam or bot callers. This helps reduce unwanted calls.

Click Bot Block Phrases to open the configuration modal.

## Bypass To Human Numbers

Define a list of phone numbers that should skip the AI entirely and be transferred directly to a target number. This is useful for VIP callers or internal staff who should always reach a human.

Click Bypass To Human Numbers to view and manage the list.

When a caller is on a landline (which cannot receive SMS), the AI cannot send text messages. This setting lets you configure what the AI says instead when it would normally send a text.

Click Landline Number SMS Prompt to configure the spoken prompt.

## Robo Call Detection

Enable robocall detection to automatically identify and block spam calls from reaching your receptionist. This reduces unnecessary charges and keeps your billing efficient.

Click Robo Call Detection to toggle it on or off. The current status is shown as a badge (On or Off).

## SMS Bot Spammers

View and manage a list of numbers that have been detected as SMS bots and blocked from SMS interactions with your receptionist.

Click SMS Bot Spammers to view the list.

## Temporary Disable

Temporarily disable your AI receptionist without deleting any configuration. When disabled, you can choose to either:

Click Temporary Disable to configure.

Connect your AI receptionist to other apps through Zapier. This allows you to automate workflows such as adding new contacts to your CRM, sending notifications to Slack, or creating tasks in your project management tool.

Click Zapier Integration and then View Details to open the Zapier configuration panel.

## Tips

- Start with the default AI model and only switch if you have a specific reason.
- Enable call recording if you want to review conversations for quality assurance.
- Use pronunciation guides for any proper nouns your AI mispronounces.

# Call Logs

Your Inbox is the central hub for viewing all call activity handled by your AI receptionist. Every inbound and outbound call is logged with a full transcript, AI-generated summary, sentiment analysis, call score, and recording.

## Accessing Call Logs

From the sidebar, click Inbox. The Inbox opens with the All Inbox tab selected by default, showing calls, voicemails, texts, and chatbot conversations in a single timeline.

To see only calls, click the Calls tab at the top of the Inbox. A count badge next to the tab name shows how many call entries are available.

## Understanding the Call List

Each entry in the call list displays:

- The caller's name (or "Unknown Caller" if no contact is saved)
- The caller's phone number
- The date and time of the call, shown in your configured time zone
- A directional badge showing whether the call was Inbound or Outbound

## Call Detail View

When you select a call, the detail panel shows the caller's name (or "Unknown Caller"), their phone number, and the call timestamp. If the caller has been added as a CRM lead, clicking the name opens their Customer Details modal where you can view and update saved contact information.

The detail panel has several tabs that appear depending on what data is available for that call:

The Recording & Transcript tab is selected by default. It contains:

The Summary & Analysis tab shows AI-generated insights:

You can configure up to three analysis scenarios from the call logs settings. Each scenario defines what information the AI should extract and in what format (Text, JSON, Boolean, or Number).

The Pricing Details tab shows a cost breakdown for the call, including AI call cost, transferred call cost, and any minutes covered by your free plan allowance. This tab is hidden for white-label accounts.

### Tickets

The Tickets tab appears when the call triggered an intake form. It shows any tickets or form submissions that were created during the conversation.

## Sharing a Call Log

To share a call log with a colleague or client, click the Share button (share icon) in the top-right corner of the call detail panel. This opens the Share Call Log modal, which provides a shareable link. The button is disabled if no shareable link is available for that call.

## Searching and Filtering

At the top of the Inbox, use the search bar to filter logs by phone number, contact name, or message content.

When viewing the Calls tab specifically, you have additional filtering controls in the toolbar:

- Filter -- Opens a panel with a Date Range picker where you can select a start and end date to narrow results. Click Apply Filters to apply, or Clear All to reset.

## Downloading Call Logs

Click the Download button in the toolbar to export your logs. A dropdown appears with options for Call Logs, Text Logs, and Voicemail Logs.

When downloading call logs, you can choose which columns to include:

1. Click Download in the toolbar.
2. Select Call Logs from the dropdown.
3. A Select Columns for Download modal appears, letting you check or uncheck individual data fields.
4. Click Select All to include every column, or pick only the ones you need.

To delete a call log, click the delete icon (trash can) on the log entry in the list, then confirm in the Confirm Delete dialog. A warning reminds you that this action cannot be undone. Click Delete to proceed or Cancel to go back.

# CRM Overview

Frontdesk AI includes a built-in CRM that automatically creates and updates customer records every time someone calls or texts your AI receptionist. You can find it in your dashboard under **CRM (Customers)**.

- **Email** -- collected during the conversation if provided
- **Lead source** -- how the customer reached you (call, text, chatbot, etc.)

# Importing and Exporting Contacts

You can bring existing contacts into Frontdesk via CSV upload, and download your CRM data as a CSV file.

## Importing contacts

### Starting an import

1. Open **CRM (Customers)** from your dashboard.
2. Click the **Import** button in the actions bar.
3. Choose your import type:
  - **Standard CSV** -- use the Frontdesk CSV format with `number`, `name`, `email`, and your custom field internal keys as column headers
  - **HubSpot Export** -- upload a HubSpot CSV export directly; Frontdesk will automatically detect columns, create any missing custom fields, and map your data

### Standard CSV format

Your CSV file must include a `number` column containing phone numbers. The `name` and `email` columns are optional but recommended.

To include custom field data, use the field's **internal key** as the column header. You can find internal keys on the **Fields & Schema** tab in your CRM.

**Requirements:**

- The `number` column is required
- Phone numbers should include the country code (for example, +1 for US numbers). Numbers without a country code default to US format.
- Custom field columns must match the internal key exactly

**To download a sample CSV** with the correct format and your custom field headers, click **Download Sample CSV** in the import dialog.

### Standard CSV import steps

1. Select **Standard CSV** on the import type screen.
2. Drag and drop your CSV file into the upload area, or click to browse.
3. Frontdesk validates your file and shows which fields were detected:
  - **Standard fields detected** -- phone number, name, email
  - **Valid custom fields detected** -- custom fields that match your CRM schema
  - **Unrecognized fields** -- columns that do not match any field (these will be skipped)
4. Review the validation results and click **Start Import**.
5. Your contacts are processed in the background. A notification confirms when the import has started.

### HubSpot import steps

1. Select **HubSpot Export** on the import type screen.
2. Drag and drop your HubSpot CSV file into the upload area.
3. Frontdesk automatically detects all columns, creates missing custom fields, maps your data, and combines first and last name fields.
4. The import starts automatically and processes in the background.

2. In the **Download Latest CRM Records** dialog, choose:
  - **Columns** -- check or uncheck the fields you want to include in the download
  - **Number of records** -- select how many records to export (for example, 100)
3. Click **Confirm** to start the download.

The export includes both standard fields (phone number, name, email, created date) and any custom fields you select. The file is delivered as a CSV that you can open in any spreadsheet application.

# Custom Fields

  - **Options** -- if you chose Pick from List, add the dropdown options
  - **Description** -- an optional note explaining what this field is for
3. Click **Save**.

The new field is immediately available across your CRM. Your AI receptionist will also be able to collect data for it during calls.

# Pipelines

Pipelines let you track deals, jobs, or any staged process on a kanban board. Each pipeline is a special field on your customer records with an ordered list of stages, a default win probability per stage, and an optional amount field for deal value.

## Creating a pipeline

1. Open **CRM (Customers)** and switch to the **Pipeline** (board) view using the view toggle in the actions bar.
2. Open the pipeline dropdown in the actions bar and choose **+ Create pipeline**. (If you have no pipelines yet, the dropdown reads **No pipelines yet**.)
3. In the **Create Pipeline** modal, enter a **Pipeline name** (for example, "Sales Pipeline").
4. Review the **Stages** list. New pipelines start with Lead (10%), Qualified (40%), and Won (100%). For each stage you can:
  - Rename it by editing the stage name.
  - Set its default win probability with the percentage input. Probabilities cannot decrease as you move down the pipeline.
  - Reorder it with the up and down arrows.
  - Remove it with the **X** button.
  - Add more stages with the **Add a stage...** input and the **Add** button.
5. Optionally pick an **Amount field**. Choose an existing number field, or type a name in **New number field name** and click **Create** to add one. The board totals this field per column and weights it by stage probability.
6. Click **Create Pipeline**, or click **Create + save view** to also pin the pipeline to your saved views row.

## Using the pipeline board

With the board view active, select a pipeline from the dropdown in the actions bar. Each stage becomes a column showing the stage name, its default probability, and the number of records in it. If the pipeline has an amount field, the column header also shows the total amount and a **Weighted** total (amount multiplied by stage probability).

- **Move a record**: drag its card from one column to another. The record's stage updates immediately.
- **Edit a card's probability**: click the percentage chip on a card, type a new value from 0 to 100, and press Enter. This overrides the stage default for that record.
- **Clear the pipeline selection**: click the **X** next to the dropdown.

## Editing and deleting a pipeline

With a pipeline selected on the board, icon buttons appear next to the dropdown:

- **Edit pipeline** (pencil) reopens the modal so you can rename the pipeline, adjust stages and probabilities, or change the amount field. Click **Save Pipeline** to apply.
- **Delete pipeline** (trash can) removes the pipeline field.

You can also edit a pipeline from the **Fields & Schema** tab, where pipelines appear alongside your other fields.

## Saving a pipeline board as a view

Saved views give you one-click access to a pipeline board:

- Click the **Save pipeline view** icon next to the pipeline dropdown, or
- Use **Create + save view** when creating a pipeline, or **Save as view** (later **Update view**) when editing one.

The view appears as a chip with a columns icon in the **Saved views** row. Views are shared with everyone in your organization. Click the **x** on the chip to delete the view (this does not delete the pipeline itself).

## Pipelines on custom objects

Custom object types can have their own pipelines too. On a custom object tab, the board dropdown groups options under **Pipelines** and **Schema fields**, plus a **+ Create pipeline** option.

## Tips

- **Keep probabilities honest** -- the weighted totals are only as useful as your stage percentages. Review them once your close rates settle.
- **One pipeline per process** -- separate sales deals from service jobs rather than mixing them in one pipeline.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Stage probabilities cannot decrease as you move down the pipeline"** -- each stage's default probability must be greater than or equal to the stage above it. Adjust the values or reorder the stages.
- **No amount totals on the board** -- the pipeline has no amount field configured. Edit the pipeline and pick one under **Amount field**.

# CRM Connections

Connections sync contacts and custom fields between Frontdesk and an external CRM, so your AI receptionist has richer context on every caller and your CRM stays up to date. HubSpot is available today; Salesforce, Pipedrive, and Zoho are coming soon.

## Connecting HubSpot

1. Open **CRM (Customers)** and click **Connections** in the tab row.
2. On the HubSpot card, click **Connect HubSpot**. You are redirected to HubSpot to authorize the connection with OAuth 2.0. Frontdesk never stores your HubSpot password.
3. After you authorize, Frontdesk's AI analyzes the fields in both systems and proposes a field mapping for you to review.

If you leave partway through setup, return to the Connections tab and click **Continue setup** on the HubSpot card.

## Reviewing the AI-suggested field mapping

The **Review field mapping** screen shows every proposed mapping, marked **AI-suggested**. No changes are made in either system until you approve. Proposals are grouped into categories:

- **Needs your input** -- mappings with a confidence below 80%. The AI mapped these but is not fully sure. Review each row, then approve, edit, or skip it. You can also click **Approve all** for the section.
- **Core fields** -- name, email, and phone are always synced and cannot be unmapped.
- **Auto-mapped** -- high-confidence matches that exist in both systems.
- **New smart variables in Frontdesk** -- fields that exist only in HubSpot. Frontdesk creates matching fields so HubSpot values land somewhere.
- **New properties in HubSpot** -- fields that exist only in Frontdesk. Frontdesk creates custom HubSpot properties to receive them.
- **Skipped** -- internal and analytics fields that are not synced.

Each row shows a confidence percentage pill (green for high, amber for medium, red for low). Click **Save as draft** to keep your edits and come back later, or **Approve** to apply the mapping. If any rows fail to save, they move to **Needs your action**, where you can edit and retry or skip them.

## Sync status and direction

Once the mapping is approved, the provider header shows a **HubSpot connected** badge (before approval it reads **Awaiting your approval**). The sync is bidirectional and runs every 15 minutes: contacts created or updated in either system flow to the other, and mapped fields stay in sync.

From the header you can also re-run the AI proposal to refresh the mapping after you add fields in either system.

## Disconnecting

1. Open the **Connections** tab and select your connected provider.
2. Click **Disconnect** in the provider header and confirm.

Contacts in both systems are preserved. You can reconnect later, and your approved mapping can be set up again.

## Other CRMs

The Connections tab lists Salesforce, Pipedrive, and Zoho under **Other CRMs** with a **Coming soon** badge. These providers cannot be connected yet.

## Tips

- **Approve promptly** -- syncing does not start until you approve the field mapping.
- **Re-run after schema changes** -- if you add fields in HubSpot or Frontdesk, re-run the AI proposal so the new fields get mapped.

# CRM API Access

The CRM API lets you read and write your customer data programmatically, so you can integrate Frontdesk with your own tools, scripts, and backends.

This feature is rolling out gradually. If you do not see the **API Integrations** button in your CRM, the API is not enabled for your account yet. Contact support to request access.

## Opening the API documentation

1. Open **CRM (Customers)** from the dashboard sidebar.
2. Click **API Integrations** in the tab row.

This opens the **CRM API Documentation** page, an in-app reference with endpoint details, parameter tables, response examples, and copy-ready code snippets in cURL, JavaScript, and Python.

## Managing your API key

Your API key lives in the **Manage Your API Key** section of the documentation page.

- **Generate**: click **Generate API Key** to create your key. The key row shows a masked value; use the eye icon to reveal it and the copy icon to copy it. The section also shows the key's status (Active or Inactive) and creation date.
- **Regenerate**: click **Regenerate** to replace the key with a new one. The old key stops working, so update any integrations that use it.
- **Delete**: click **Delete** to revoke the key entirely.

Keep your API key secure. It provides full access to your customer data, so do not commit it to public repositories or ship it in client-side code. If it is ever exposed, regenerate it immediately.

## Authentication

Every request must include your API key in a header. Two forms are accepted:

- `X-API-Key: your-api-key-here`
- `Authorization: Bearer your-api-key-here`

The base URL for customer endpoints is `https://www.247aireceptionist.com/api/v1/customers`.

## What the API covers

At a high level, the API supports:

- **List customers** -- `GET /customers` returns a paginated list with `page` and `pageSize` parameters, plus searching, sorting, and filtering by custom field values (for example, `smart.status[in]=active,pending` or `smart.revenue_impact[gt]=5000`).
- **Get a customer** -- `GET /customers/{customer_id}` fetches a single record.
- **Look up a customer** -- `GET /customers/lookup` finds records by phone number or email.
- **Create a customer** -- `POST /customers` with name, email, phone, and a `variables` object for custom field values. This endpoint does not check for duplicates, so look the customer up first if you need to avoid them.
- **Update a customer** -- `PATCH /customers/{customer_id}` changes core fields or custom field values.
- **Delete a customer** -- `DELETE /customers/{customer_id}` removes the record. You can also delete a single field value with the `variableKey` query parameter.
- **Custom objects** -- endpoints for creating, listing, updating, and deleting custom object types and their records, plus linking and unlinking objects to contacts.

For exact request and response shapes, use the in-app reference. It is always current with your account and includes runnable examples for each endpoint.

## Tips

- **Use lookup before create** -- pair `GET /customers/lookup` with `POST /customers` to avoid duplicate records for the same phone number.
- **Filter server-side** -- custom field filters on the list endpoint are faster than pulling every page and filtering in your own code.

# Enrolling Contacts

Enrollment determines which contacts enter an outbound campaign and when. You configure this through the **Enrollment Rules** modal, which opens automatically when you create a new outbound campaign or when you click the trigger card in the builder.

## Selecting a Trigger

The first step is choosing a trigger type. Open the **Select Trigger** dropdown to see the available options:

### Contact Triggers

- **Contact Created** -- The workflow runs whenever a new contact is added to your CRM (e.g., from a phone call, form submission, or manual entry).
- **Contact Updated** -- The workflow runs whenever an existing contact's information changes.
- **Contact Conditional** -- The workflow runs when a contact matches specific conditions you define. This trigger **requires** at least one enrollment condition (see below).

### Custom Object Triggers

If your account uses custom objects, additional trigger options appear for each object type:

- **[Object Name] Created** -- Triggered when a new record of that object type is created.
- **[Object Name] Updated** -- Triggered when an existing record of that object type is updated.

## Enrollment Conditions

Below the trigger selector, the **Enrollment Conditions** section lets you filter which contacts (or objects) actually enter the outbound campaign.

- For **Contact Conditional** triggers, at least one condition is **required**.
- For all other triggers, conditions are **optional** but recommended to avoid enrolling every contact.

### Building Conditions

Enrollment conditions are organized into **rule groups**. Click **Add Your First Rule** to create the first group, then build each condition inside it:

1. **Select a field** -- Choose any CRM variable (e.g., City, Lead Source, Subscription Status).
2. **Choose an operator** -- Options include equals, not equals, contains, is empty, is not empty, and more.
3. **Set a value** -- Enter the value to match (not required for "is empty" / "is not empty" operators).

Conditions within the same group are combined with **AND**: a contact must satisfy every condition in the group to match it.

### Multiple Rule Groups (OR logic)

Click **Add Rule Group** to add more groups. Groups are combined with **OR**: a contact enrolls if it matches **any** group. This lets you target several distinct audiences with one campaign. For example:

- **Rule Group 1**: Lead Source equals "Web Form" AND City equals "Austin"
- **Rule Group 2**: Subscription Status equals "Expired"

A contact matching either group enrolls. All of your rule groups are saved when you click **Save Rules**; groups with no conditions are discarded. Use **Remove Group** on a group's header to delete it.

### Saving Rules

Click **Save Rules** to apply your trigger and enrollment conditions. Click **Cancel** to discard changes.

The **Save Rules** button is disabled until you have:

- Selected a trigger type
- Added at least one valid condition (for conditional triggers)

## Automatic vs. Manual Enrollment

### Automatic Enrollment

Once an outbound campaign is activated, contacts are enrolled automatically as the trigger fires. For example:

- A **Contact Created** trigger enrolls every new contact.
- A **Contact Conditional** trigger enrolls contacts only when they match your conditions after being created or updated.

### Enrollment on Activation

When you activate an outbound campaign, the system checks for existing contacts that match your enrollment rules. If matches are found, the **Activate Outbound Campaign** modal shows:

- The number of **qualified leads** found.
- A checkbox to **Run this outbound campaign on these leads immediately**.

Check the box and click **Activate** to enroll those existing contacts right away, in addition to enabling automatic enrollment for future contacts.

If no contacts currently match, the workflow activates in "waiting" mode and will enroll future contacts as they qualify.

### Deactivating an Outbound Campaign

Toggle the workflow off at any time from the workflow card or from within the builder. Deactivating a workflow stops new enrollments but does not cancel runs already in progress.

## Tips for Effective Enrollment

- **Be specific with conditions** -- Broad triggers like "Contact Created" with no conditions will enroll every new contact. Add conditions to target the right audience.
- **Test with a small group** -- When activating, review the qualified lead count before checking "Run on leads immediately."
- **Use conditional triggers for re-engagement** -- Set up a "Contact Conditional" trigger with conditions like "Last Call Date is more than 30 days ago" to re-engage inactive contacts.

# Campaign Variables

Variables let you personalize outbound campaign content for each lead. You define a variable once, insert it in your campaign text as `{{variableName}}`, and Frontdesk fills in the right value for every contact when the campaign runs.

## Opening Variable Management

1. Open your outbound campaigns dashboard and select a campaign.
2. Click **Variables** in the sidebar.
3. The **Variable Management** page opens, showing how many variables the campaign has under **Your Variables**.

## How variables work

Anywhere your campaign uses text (greetings, scripts, prompts), you can insert a variable with double curly braces:

```
Hi {{firstName}}, this is a reminder about your {{serviceType}} appointment.
```

When the campaign contacts a lead, each variable is replaced with that lead's value. Variables come in two kinds:

- **Mandatory** -- a value must be provided for every lead. There is no fallback.
- **Optional** -- if a lead has no value, the variable's **Default Value** is used instead.

## Creating a variable

1. Click **Add Variable**.
2. In the **Create New Variable** modal, enter a **Variable Name**. Use a unique identifier without spaces (e.g., `firstName`, `appointmentDate`).
3. Leave **This variable is mandatory** checked if every lead must supply a value.
4. If you uncheck it, a **Default Value** field appears. Enter the fallback text to use when a lead has no value. Optional variables require a default.
5. Click **Create Variable**.

The variable is saved to the campaign immediately and is ready to use in your content.

## Editing a variable

1. Find the variable in the list and click its edit action.
2. You can change whether it is mandatory and update the default value. The variable's name cannot be changed after creation.
3. Click **Update Variable**.

## Deleting a variable

Click the delete action on a variable. If the variable is not referenced anywhere, it is removed right away.

If the variable is currently used in campaign fields, a **Variable in use** dialog lists exactly which fields reference it and asks you to confirm. If you proceed, the variable is deleted and every `{{variableName}}` placeholder is removed from those fields automatically, so your campaign text never speaks a raw placeholder aloud.

## Tips

- **Name variables for readers** -- `appointmentDate` is easier to spot in a script than `var2`.
- **Prefer optional variables with sensible defaults** for data you don't always have. A default like "your upcoming appointment" keeps the sentence natural when the specific value is missing.
- **Keep mandatory variables to true requirements** -- every lead you enroll must have a value for each mandatory variable, so only mark a variable mandatory when the message makes no sense without it.
- **Check before deleting** -- read the "Variable in use" list carefully. Removing a placeholder can leave a sentence that needs rewording.
