1. Navigate to **Analytics & Insights** from the sidebar.
2. Click the **Customer Insights** tab (the third tab, with a people icon).

## Chart Builder Dashboard

The Customer Insights tab displays the **Chart Builder Dashboard**, which lets you create custom charts from your CRM data.

The chart builder uses your CRM variables (the same fields used in web forms and by the AI receptionist) to generate visualizations. You can explore trends across any contact property you track.

### How It Works

The chart builder pulls from your CRM contact data and the smart variables (customer information fields) you have defined. This means every field your receptionist collects -- from names and phone numbers to custom fields like "Service Type" or "Budget Range" -- can be visualized.

Available chart types include pie, bar, line, area, and funnel charts, as well as metric cards, data tables, text blocks, and heading elements.

## Date Range

Unlike the Overview and Call Analytics tabs, the Customer Insights tab does not use the date range picker. Charts are generated from your full CRM dataset.

## Exporting

You can export the Customer Insights dashboard as a PDF using the **Export** button in the toolbar. The export captures the current state of your chart builder dashboard.

## Tips

- **Add CRM variables for richer insights** -- The more customer information fields you define, the more dimensions you can chart. Consider adding fields like lead source, service category, or location.
- **Use with sequences** -- Combine insights from this tab with automated sequences. For example, if you notice a high concentration of contacts from a specific city, create a targeted sequence for that segment.
- **Regular review** -- Check Customer Insights periodically to spot trends in your customer base, such as growth in specific segments or changes in common inquiry types.

## Next Steps

- Analytics Dashboard -- Call volume, peak hours, and duration charts.
- CRM Overview -- Managing your contact database and smart variables.

# Chatbot Widget Overview

The Chatbot Widget lets you add an AI-powered chat assistant to your website. Visitors can ask questions, get instant answers, and connect with a human operator when needed -- all without leaving your site.

## Video walkthrough

https://www.youtube.com/embed/Phf8ctv3KVQ

## What the Chatbot Does

- Greets visitors automatically with a customizable message
- Answers questions using your AI receptionist's knowledge base
- Collects lead information around the clock
- Hands off conversations to a human operator based on escalation rules you define
- Plays notification sounds so you never miss a new conversation

## Where to Find It

In your dashboard, navigate to **Website Widget**. You will see two tabs at the top:

- **Website Chatbot** -- the chat widget covered in this guide
- **Website Voicebot** -- a separate click-to-call widget (see Website Call Widget)

Select **Website Chatbot** to open the chatbot configuration page.

## Page Layout

The chatbot configuration page is divided into a left-side navigation panel and a live preview on the right. The navigation panel has six sections:

1. **Look & Feel** -- Theme, colors, widget position, and mobile margins
2. **Content** -- Business name, greeting message, popup message, and display names
3. **AI Brain** -- The AI prompt that controls how your chatbot responds
4. **Escalation Rules** -- Conditions that trigger a handoff to a human operator
5. **Behavior** -- Auto-open settings for the widget
6. **Sounds & Alerts** -- Notification sounds for new conversations and messages

Click any section in the left navigation to jump to its settings. A live preview of your chatbot updates as you make changes.

## Getting Started

1. Open the **Website Widget** page and select the **Website Chatbot** tab.
2. Configure your chatbot using the six sections described above.
3. Click **Save** at the top of the page to save your settings.
4. Copy the embed code from the **Add your chatbot to your website** banner and paste it into your site (see Installing the Chatbot on Your Website for details).
5. Check the **My Chatbot is Live!** checkbox once the code is on your site.

## Activation Steps

The banner at the top of the page shows a three-step progress indicator:

1. **Configure** -- Set up your chatbot appearance and behavior
2. **Copy Code** -- Copy the embed snippet
3. **Embed on Site** -- Paste the code into your website

You can also click **Installation Guides** for platform-specific instructions, or **Email My Developer** to send the embed code directly to your web developer.

Once all three steps are complete, your chatbot is live and ready to engage visitors.

## Saving Changes

After making any configuration changes, click the **Save** button to apply them. The chatbot preview refreshes automatically.

## Next Steps

- Customizing Your Chatbot -- Adjust appearance, content, AI behavior, escalation rules, and sounds
- Installing the Chatbot on Your Website -- Platform-specific installation instructions

# Customizing Your Chatbot

This guide walks through each configuration section of the Chatbot Widget. All settings are found on the **Website Widget** page under the **Website Chatbot** tab.

After making changes in any section, click **Save** at the top of the page to apply them.

---

## Look & Feel

Controls the visual appearance of your chatbot widget.

### Theme

Choose between two themes:

- **Light** -- A bright, clean appearance
- **Dark** -- A darker color scheme

### Colors

The available color options change based on your selected theme:

- **Light theme** -- Pick a **Primary Color** and a **Secondary Color** from six preset swatches (blue, purple, green, red, amber, pink).
- **Dark theme** -- Pick an **Accent Color** from seven preset swatches (the six above plus black).

### Widget Position

Place the chat bubble in one of two corners of the page:

- **Bottom Left**
- **Bottom Right**

### Mobile Margins

Expand the **Mobile margins** section to fine-tune how the widget appears on screens 768 px wide or narrower. You can set individual pixel values for **Top**, **Right**, **Bottom**, and **Left** margins (0--100 px).

---

## Content

Controls the text and branding visitors see in the chat window.

### Business Name

Enter your business name (up to 50 characters). This appears in the chat header.

### Greeting Message

The first message visitors see when they open the chat (up to 200 characters). The default is:
> Hi! How can we help you today?

### Popup Message

A short teaser shown on the chat bubble before visitors open the widget (up to 100 characters). The default is:
> Have a question? Chat with us!

### Display Names

Customize how the AI and human operators appear to visitors:

- **AI Agent Name** -- Give your AI a friendly name (e.g., "Maya"). This is optional.
- **Operator Names** -- Map each human operator's username to a customer-facing display name. Click **Add Operator** to add a new mapping. Select the operator from the dropdown, then type the display name in the **Display as...** field. Remove a mapping with the delete icon.

---

## AI Brain

This section embeds the same AI prompt editor used elsewhere in your dashboard. It controls the instructions, personality, and knowledge your chatbot draws on when responding to visitors.

The AI Brain section uses the same AI Prompt editor as the voice receptionist's Custom Commands on the Overview page, allowing you to configure AI behavior consistently across both voice and chatbot interfaces.

---

## Escalation Rules

Define scenarios where the AI should hand off a conversation to a human operator. You can create up to 10 rules.

### Creating a Rule

1. Click **Add Rule**.
2. Fill in the form:
  - **Status** -- Toggle the rule **Enabled** or **Disabled**.
  - **Title** -- A short name for the rule (e.g., "Sales Inquiry").
  - **Scenario Description** -- Describe when this rule should trigger (e.g., "Escalate when customer asks about pricing, sales, or enterprise plans").
  - **Response Message** -- The message shown to the visitor while the handoff happens (e.g., "Ok wait, someone would join soon.").
  - **Keywords (comma-separated)** -- Optional keywords that help the AI identify the scenario.
  - **Decline/Offline Intake Workflow** -- Optional. Select an intake workflow to run if the request is declined or no operator is available.
3. Click **Save**.

### Managing Rules

Each rule card shows its title, status (**Active** or **Off**), description, and keyword tags. Hover over a rule to reveal:

- **Edit** (pencil icon) -- Opens the rule for editing
- **Delete** (trash icon) -- Removes the rule

The counter at the top shows how many rules you have configured out of the maximum (e.g., "3 of 10 rules configured").

---

## Behavior

### Auto-Open Widget

Toggle this setting to have the chat window open automatically after a delay on desktop devices.

- **Enabled** -- The widget opens on its own after the specified delay.
- **Disabled** -- Visitors must click the chat bubble to open it.

When enabled, use the **Delay** slider to set how many seconds to wait before opening (5--120 seconds). The default is 30 seconds.

This setting applies to desktop only; it does not auto-open on mobile.

---

## Sounds & Alerts

Configure notification sounds for two audiences: your dashboard and the widget on your website.

### Dashboard

- **New Conversations** -- Play a sound when a new chatbot conversation starts.
- **New Messages** -- Play a sound for each new message in existing conversations.

### Widget (on your website)

- **New Conversations** -- Play a sound on the embedded widget for new conversations.
- **New Messages** -- Play a sound on the embedded widget for new messages.

For each notification type:

1. Toggle it on or off with the switch.
2. When enabled, select a sound from the dropdown.
3. Click **Preview** to hear the selected sound.

You can set the sound to **Mute** if you want the notification enabled (for visual indicators) without an audible alert.

# Installing the Chatbot on Your Website

After configuring your chatbot on the **Website Widget** page, you need to add a small code snippet to your website so the widget appears for visitors.

---

## Step 1: Copy the Embed Code

1. Open the **Website Widget** page and select the **Website Chatbot** tab.
2. At the top of the page, find the **Add your chatbot to your website** banner.
3. Click **Copy Embed Code**. The snippet is now on your clipboard.

If your chatbot is already live and you need the code again, click **Show Embed Code** to reveal the banner.

---

## Step 2: Add the Code to Your Website

Paste the embed code just before the closing `</body>` tag on every page where you want the chatbot to appear. The exact steps depend on your website platform.

### HTML / Other

1. Open your website's HTML file (usually `index.html` or the main template).
2. Find the closing `</body>` tag.
3. Paste the embed code just before `</body>`.
4. Save and upload the file to your hosting provider.
5. The chatbot widget will initialize automatically when visitors load the page.

### WordPress

1. Log in to your WordPress admin dashboard.
2. Install and activate the **Insert Headers and Footers** plugin (or **WPCode**).
3. Go to **Settings > Insert Headers and Footers** (or **Code Snippets > Header & Footer**).
4. Paste the embed code into the **Scripts in Footer** section.
5. Click **Save**. Your chatbot will now appear on every page.

### Shopify

1. Log in to your Shopify admin panel.
2. Go to **Online Store > Themes**.
3. Click **...** on your current theme, then **Edit Code**.
4. Open the `theme.liquid` file.
5. Paste the embed code just before the closing `</body>` tag.
6. Click **Save**. Your chatbot will appear on your store.

### Wix

1. Log in to your Wix dashboard.
2. Go to **Settings > Custom Code** (or use the Wix Editor: **Add > Embed Code**).
3. Click **+ Add Custom Code**.
4. Paste the embed code.
5. Set placement to **Body - End** and apply to **All Pages**.
6. Click **Apply**. Your chatbot is now live.

### Squarespace

1. Log in to your Squarespace admin.
2. Go to **Settings > Advanced > Code Injection**.
3. Paste the embed code into the **Footer** field.
4. Click **Save**. Your chatbot will appear site-wide.

---

# Website Call Widget

The Website Call Widget (also called the Website Voicebot) adds a click-to-call button to your website. Visitors click the button to start a voice call with your AI receptionist directly from their browser -- no phone number needed.

---

## Where to Find It

1. In your dashboard, navigate to **Website Widget**.
2. Select the **Website Voicebot** tab at the top of the page.

This opens the **Chatwave Embeddable Widget Customizer**, where you design and configure your call button.

---

## Page Layout

The customizer is split into two areas:

- **Left panel** -- Configuration tabs and settings
- **Right panel** -- A live preview of your widget and the embed code

Three tabs organize the settings:

| Tab         | What it controls                                                                         |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Presets** | Widget type, position type, and pre-made designs                                         |
| **Style**   | Position, icon, button, container, background, border, shadow, animation, and brand icon |
| **Text**    | Primary and secondary text, feedback messages, font size, text color, and floating text  |

---

## Presets Tab

### Widget Type

Choose how the call button looks:

- **Contained** -- A larger widget with a container around the button and text
- **Compact** -- A smaller, minimal button

### Position Type

Choose how the widget behaves on the page:

- **Fixed Position** -- The widget stays in place while the visitor scrolls
- **Static Position** -- The widget sits inline with your page content

### Pre-made Designs

Select from a gallery of ready-made designs. Clicking a preset applies its colors, layout, and styling instantly. You can further customize any preset using the **Style** and **Text** tabs.

---

## Style Tab

### Position Settings

Available when **Fixed Position** is selected. Set the widget's placement on the page:

- **Horizontal Position** -- Left or Right, with a pixel offset
- **Vertical Position** -- Top or Bottom, with a pixel offset

### Icon Settings

- **Icon Type** -- Choose from **Phone**, **Microphone**, or **Voice Note**
- **Icon Size** -- Adjust the icon size in pixels
- **Icon Position** -- Place the icon at the **Start**, **Center**, or **End** of the button
- **Icon Color** -- Pick any color using the color picker

### Button Style

Customize the call button itself:

- **Width** and **Height**
- **Background** -- Solid color or gradient (with start color, end color, and direction), plus a separate color shown while in-call
- **Border Radius** -- Round the corners individually
- **Border** -- Width, style (solid, dashed, dotted), and color
- **Box Shadow** -- Enable/disable, blur, spread, color, and opacity

### Container Style

Available in **Contained** mode. Customize the outer wrapper:

- **Width** and **Height**
- **Background** -- Solid or gradient
- **Border Radius**, **Border**, **Box Shadow** -- Same options as the button
- **Padding** -- Top, right, bottom, left (with a link toggle to change all sides at once)
- **Side Animation** -- None, Voice Wave, or Custom Image (with a URL and size control)

### Brand Icon

Upload or link to an image (e.g., your logo) that appears alongside the call button.

### Floating Text

Enable a line of text beneath the widget (e.g., "Powered by YourBrand"). When enabled, you can set:

- **Text** content
- **Link URL**
- **Font Size**
- **Text Color**

---

## Text Tab

Customize the labels and messages visitors see:

- **Primary Text** -- The main label on the widget (e.g., your business name)
- **Secondary Text** -- Supporting text (e.g., "Start a call")
- **Font Size** and **Text Color**
- **Feedback Messages** -- Messages shown during different call states:
  * **Setting Up** message
  * **Click** message
  * **Connecting** message

---

## Saving and Embedding

1. Click **Save Changes** in the top-right corner of the customizer. Your unique embed code is generated after the first save.
2. The embed code appears in the right panel. Click **Copy** to copy it to your clipboard.
3. Paste the embed code into your website's HTML, just before the closing `</body>` tag.

If you have not saved yet, you will see a prompt: "Save settings to get your embed code."

# AI Avatar

The Avatar feature gives your AI receptionist a human-like video presence that visitors can talk to on your website. You choose an appearance, set a greeting, customize the widget, and embed a short code snippet on your site.

If you don't see **Avatar** in your sidebar, it isn't enabled for your account yet. Contact support to request access.

## The Avatar page

Open **Avatar** in the sidebar. The page has a section menu on the left (**Appearance**, **Settings**, **Widget**, **Embed Code**), the active section in the center, and a **Preview** card on the right. A **Save changes** button under the menu saves your configuration; remember to click it after making changes.

## Appearance

Pick the face and look of your avatar:

1. Browse the avatar gallery, or use the **Search avatars** box to filter by name.
2. Click an avatar to select it.

Admins can also create a custom avatar:

1. Click **Create custom**.
2. Enter an avatar name (3 to 50 characters).
3. Upload an image file or switch to providing an image URL.
4. Submit to create the avatar. It appears in your gallery and is selected automatically.

You can delete a custom avatar with its delete action; deletion is permanent. Use the refresh button if a newly created avatar doesn't show up.

## Settings

- **Business name** -- the name the avatar represents. Defaults to your organization's business name.
- **Greeting message** -- what the avatar says when a conversation starts (e.g., "Hi! Welcome to our business. How can I help you today?").
- **Avatar AI prompt** -- the instructions that control how the avatar behaves in conversation.

The avatar speaks with your AI receptionist voice, so it stays consistent with your phone and chat channels.

## Widget

Control how the widget looks on your website:

- **Popup message** -- the short teaser shown next to the widget (default: "Chat with our AI avatar for instant help!").
- **Widget shape** -- circular or box.
- **Position** -- bottom right or bottom left of the page.
- **Margins** -- pixel offsets that fine-tune where the widget sits.

The Preview card on the right reflects your current shape, position, and margin settings.

## Testing and sharing

From the Preview card you can:

- **Test now** -- opens a live preview session where you talk to the avatar. Use the mute button to toggle your microphone and close the modal to end the session.
- **Copy share link** -- copies a link you can send to teammates so they can try the avatar without logging in.
- **Preview widget on page** -- shows the widget floating on the dashboard, exactly as it will appear on your site. Click again to hide it.

Avatar sessions consume 50 credits per minute of conversation. Click **How do credits work?** at the top of the page for details. If you run out of credits, the test session won't start and you'll be prompted to add credits or upgrade.

## Embed Code

The **Embed Code** section generates a two-line script tag tied to your agent. Click the copy button and paste the snippet just before the closing `</body>` tag of your website. The panel includes step-by-step guides for common platforms, including WordPress and Wix.

## Troubleshooting

- **"No Avatar Selected"** -- select an avatar in Appearance before testing, sharing, or saving.
- **Test session won't start** -- you may be out of credits. Check the credits page or upgrade your plan.
- **Avatar Name Required / Image Required** -- custom avatars need a name of at least 3 characters and either an uploaded image or an image URL.
- **Widget not appearing on your site** -- confirm the embed snippet is on the page, and that you copied it while the correct agent was selected.

# Website Builder Overview

The Website Builder generates a complete business website for you and lets you refine it by chatting with the AI. You can build a site from a short description, or clone your existing site and rebuild it with your AI chatbot and contact form included. When you are happy with it, publish to a free Frontdesk subdomain or connect your own domain.

If you don't see **Website/SEO AI** in your sidebar, it isn't enabled for your account yet. Contact support to request access.

## Generating your first website

Open **Website/SEO AI** in the sidebar. If you have no website yet, you'll see the creation screen with two modes:

- **Build from scratch** -- describe the site you want in the text box (e.g., "a modern landing page for my plumbing business with a booking section") and click the send button.
- **Clone existing site** -- paste your current website URL and click **Clone & Build**. Frontdesk pulls your content and branding, then rebuilds the site. This works best with publicly accessible sites; login-gated pages can't be read.

Generation takes a few minutes. A progress screen shows each stage, including "Designing layout & theme."

## Editing with chat

Once your site exists, the builder shows three tabs on the left (**Design**, **Versions**, **Domain**) with a live preview on the right. You can drag the divider between them to resize the panels.

On the **Design** tab, type what you want changed and send it. Every edit creates a new version and updates the preview. You can also attach images to use on the site. If you're not sure where to start, click one of the **Quick Suggestions**, such as:

- Make it look more premium
- Add an FAQ section
- Use a darker color scheme
- Add a testimonials section

Each account has an edit allowance; the panel shows how many edits you have used.

## Versions

The **Versions** tab lists every version of your site, newest first. The most recent one is labeled **Latest**, and the version currently on your published site is tagged as live. For each version you can:

- **Preview** it in the right-hand pane.
- **Restore** it (or **Revert** in the chat history) to bring an older version back as the latest draft. Restoring never publishes automatically; review it, then publish when ready.

At the bottom of the Versions tab, **Start Over** deletes the current website so you can generate a new one from scratch. Previous versions are preserved and can be recovered. Start-overs are limited per day, and the counter under the button shows your usage.

## Publishing

Click **Publish** to put the currently previewed version live.

The first time you publish, the **Choose Your Staging URL** modal asks you to claim a permanent subdomain on **.myaifrontdesk.com** (e.g., `your-business-name.myaifrontdesk.com`). You can't change this later, so pick carefully. After you click **Claim & Continue**, the SSL certificate activates, usually within 1 to 3 minutes. The site publishes automatically once the certificate is ready, or you can click **Check Status** to trigger it manually.

On later publishes, a confirmation modal appears. Click **Yes, Publish** to replace the current live version.

## Custom domain

The **Domain** tab manages where your site lives:

1. Under the custom domain section, enter your domain (e.g., `www.mybusiness.com`) and click **Connect**.
2. Frontdesk shows a **CNAME** record. Add it at your domain registrar (GoDaddy, Namecheap, Cloudflare, etc.).
3. Click **Verify & Connect**. DNS propagation can take a few minutes, so retry if it isn't detected immediately.
4. After verification, the SSL certificate provisions in 1 to 5 minutes. Click **Check Status** to confirm, and you'll see "Your custom domain is connected!"

You can disconnect the custom domain or the staging URL from the same tab.

## Troubleshooting

- **"This subdomain is already taken"** -- another account claimed that staging slug. Choose a different one.
- **"DNS record not detected yet"** -- the CNAME hasn't propagated. Wait a few minutes and click **Verify & Connect** again.
- **Clone fails on your URL** -- confirm the site is publicly reachable and includes the `https://` scheme. Protected or login-gated sites can't be cloned.
- **Publish button missing** -- you need at least one generated version. Generate or restore a version first.

# Voice Library

The Voice Library is where you browse, preview, and select the voice your AI receptionist uses on calls. You can also switch to the **Clone Voice** tab to create a custom voice (see Voice Cloning).

## Video walkthrough

https://www.youtube.com/embed/RsANaqRIKyg

---

## Where to Find It

In your dashboard, navigate to **Voice Library**. The page header reads "Voice Library" with the description "Access and explore your Voice Library in minutes!"

Two tabs appear at the top:

- **Voice Library** -- Browse and select from available voices
- **Clone Voice** -- Create your own voice clone

---

## Browsing Voices

The Voice Library tab is organized into three sections, displayed from top to bottom:

### Current Voice

Shows the voice (or voices) currently assigned to your receptionist. If your receptionist handles both English and other languages, you may see two cards here -- one for each.

### Featured Voices

A curated selection of popular voices. These appear on the first page only.

### All Voices

The full catalog of available voices, displayed as a paginated grid. Use the pagination controls at the bottom to navigate through pages.

---

## Searching and Filtering

### Search

Type in the **Search voices...** field above the **All Voices** section to find voices by name. Searching clears any active filters.

### Filters

Click the **Filters** button next to the search field to open the filter panel. You can filter by:

| Filter       | Description                                                                       |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Provider** | The voice synthesis provider (e.g., ElevenLabs, Cartesia, OpenAI, Deepgram, Rime) |
| **Gender**   | Male, Female, or All                                                              |
| **Language** | English, or other supported languages                                             |
| **Accent**   | Regional accents (varies by provider)                                             |

Active filters appear as tags below the search bar. Click the **X** on any tag to remove that filter, or click **Clear all** to reset everything.

---

## Previewing a Voice

Each voice is displayed as a card showing the voice name, provider, language, and other details. Click the play button on any card to hear a sample. Only one voice plays at a time -- starting a new preview stops the previous one.

---

## Selecting a Voice

To assign a voice to your receptionist, click the voice card and it will be applied. The selected voice card is highlighted to show it is active.

---

## Voice Configuration

Some voices offer additional tuning options. Click the settings icon on a voice card to open the **Voice Configuration** modal. Available options vary by provider:

### Cartesia voices

- **Voice Model** -- Select a specific model variant
- **Speed** -- Adjust speaking speed
- **Emotion Name** -- Choose an emotion (e.g., neutral, happy)
- **Emotion Level** -- Set the intensity of the emotion

### OpenAI voices

- **Voice Model**
- **Speed**
- **Accent** -- Choose a regional accent
- **Emotional Range**
- **Intonation**
- **Impression**
- **Tone**
- **Whispering**
- **Voice Prompt** -- Enter a free-text prompt to describe how the voice should sound (e.g., "Speak in a cheerful and positive tone")

### Rime voices (Arcana model)

- **Temperature** -- Slider from Deterministic to Creative

### Rime voices (MistV2 model)

- **Speed** -- Slider from Faster to Slower
- **Custom Pauses** -- Toggle on/off
- **Custom Pronunciations** -- Toggle on/off

After adjusting settings, click **OK** to apply them.

---

## How Credits Work

Click the **How Credits Work** button in the top-right corner to open a modal explaining voice credit usage and costs. This button is available on non-reseller accounts that have an active phone number.

---

## Next Steps

- Voice Cloning -- Create a custom voice from an audio recording
- Pronunciation Guide -- Teach your receptionist how to pronounce specific words

# Pronunciation Guide

The Pronunciation Guide lets you teach your AI receptionist how to say specific words or names. This is useful for business names, product names, proper nouns, or any term the AI might mispronounce.

---

## Where to Find It

Go to the **Overview** page, select the **Configure** tab, expand the **Tweak Advanced Settings** section, and find the **Pronunciation Guides** card.

---

## How It Works

Each pronunciation entry consists of two parts:

- **Word** -- The word or phrase as it is normally written (e.g., "New York")
- **Pronunciation** -- The phonetic spelling the AI should use (e.g., "/nju: 'jo:rk/")

The AI reads the phonetic version instead of the written word during calls.

---

## Adding a Pronunciation

1. In the pronunciation form, you will see fields for **Word** and **Pronunciation**.
2. Enter the word in the **Word** field.
3. Enter the phonetic pronunciation in the **Pronunciation** field.
4. To add more entries, click **Add Row**.
5. Click **Save** to submit your entries.

### Auto-Generate with AI

You do not have to write phonetics by hand. After typing a word, click the robot icon next to the row. The system will auto-generate an IPA (International Phonetic Alphabet) pronunciation for that word.

### Listen Before Saving

Click the speaker icon next to either the **Word** or **Pronunciation** field to hear how the AI will say it. This lets you verify the pronunciation sounds correct before saving.

---

## Phonetic Examples

Here are a few examples of IPA-format pronunciations:

| Word     | Pronunciation |
| -------- | ------------- |
| New York | /nju: 'jo:rk/ |
| Paris    | /'perIs/      |
| Tokyo    | /'to:.kio:/   |

---

## Managing Existing Pronunciations

All saved pronunciations appear in a table below the form with three columns:

| Column            | Description                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **Word**          | The original word                   |
| **Pronunciation** | The phonetic version                |
| **Action**        | A delete button to remove the entry |

- Click the speaker icon in the **Word** or **Pronunciation** column to hear that value spoken aloud.
- Click the delete icon in the **Action** column to remove a pronunciation entry. This takes effect immediately.

---

## Tips

- Use IPA notation for the most accurate results.
- Test pronunciations with the speaker icon before saving.
- If the auto-generated phonetic does not sound right, edit it manually and test again.
- You can add multiple entries at once by clicking **Add Row** for each new word, then saving them all together.

## Next Steps

- Voice Library -- Browse and select from all available voices
- Voice Cloning -- Create a custom voice from an audio recording

# Voice Cloning

Voice Cloning lets you create a custom voice for your AI receptionist by uploading an audio recording or recording one directly in your browser. The cloned voice can then be selected in the Voice Library and used on calls.

---

## Where to Find It

1. In your dashboard, navigate to **Voice Library**.
2. Select the **Clone Voice** tab at the top of the page.

---

## Creating a Voice Clone

The **Create Custom Voice** form has four fields and an audio source selector.

### 1. Voice Name

Enter a name for your custom voice (required). This is how the voice will appear in your library.

### 2. Description

Provide a short description of the voice (required). For example, "Warm and professional female voice for customer service."

### 3. Voice Provider

Choose which provider processes the clone. Select one of:

- **Elevenlabs**
- **Cartesia**

Click the provider name to toggle between them.

### 4. Audio Source

Provide the voice sample using one of two methods:

- **Select File** -- Click to upload a `.wav` or `.mp3` file from your computer (maximum 10 MB).
- **Start Recording** -- Click to record directly using your microphone. The button turns red and pulses while recording. Click **Stop Recording** when finished.

After uploading or recording, you will see a confirmation:

- Uploaded files display the file name.
- Recordings display an audio player so you can review the clip. Click the **X** button to discard and re-record.

### 5. Submit

Click **Create Voice Clone** to upload your audio and begin the cloning process. A success message confirms when the voice has been created and attached to your receptionist.

---

## Your Cloned Voices

After creating one or more clones, a **Your Cloned Voices** section appears below the creation form. Each cloned voice is shown as a card, just like voices in the main library.

From these cards you can:

- **Preview** -- Play a sample of the cloned voice
- **Select** -- Apply the voice to your receptionist
- **Delete** -- Remove the cloned voice

---

## Requirements and Limits

- **Supported formats**: WAV, MP3
- **Maximum file size**: 10 MB
- For best results, use a clear recording with minimal background noise
- Speak naturally for at least 10--15 seconds to give the provider enough data

---

## Next Steps

- Voice Library -- Browse and select from all available voices
- Pronunciation Guide -- Customize how your receptionist says specific words

# Notification Settings

Notification settings let you control when and how you receive alerts about calls, voicemails, texts, chatbot conversations, calendar events, and other activity handled by your AI receptionist.

## Video walkthrough

https://www.youtube.com/embed/FVCUq0qKuY0

---

## Where to Find It

In your dashboard, navigate to the **Notifications** page (accessible from the sidebar). The page header shows a bell icon and the title **Manage Notifications**.

---

## How Notifications Work

Each notification is defined by three things:

1. **Type** -- What event triggers the notification
2. **Method** -- How the notification is delivered (email or SMS)
3. **Recipients** -- Who receives it (one or more email addresses or phone numbers)

You can create multiple notifications for the same event type. For example, you could send an email to your office manager and an SMS to your personal phone whenever a call comes in.

---

## Notification Types

| Type          | What it covers                                                            |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Call**      | Completed inbound or outbound calls                                       |
| **Voicemail** | Voicemail messages left by callers                                        |
| **Text**      | SMS/text messages received through the texting platform                   |
| **Robocall**  | Detected robocalls or spam calls                                          |
| **Chatbot**   | Conversations from the website chatbot widget                             |
| **Calendar**  | Calendar events and appointment bookings                                  |
| **Scenario**  | Custom scenarios you define (e.g., "VIP Caller," "After-Hours Emergency") |
| **Intake**    | Intake workflow completions                                               |

---

## Delivery Methods

- **Email** -- Sends a formatted email to the specified addresses
- **SMS** -- Sends a text message to the specified phone numbers

SMS notifications may require a Pro subscription depending on your plan.

---

## Creating a Notification

1. Click the button to create a new notification.
2. In the modal, fill in:
  - **Type** -- Select the event type from the dropdown.
  - **Method** -- Choose **Email** or **SMS**.
  - **Recipient** -- Enter one or more email addresses or phone numbers (comma-separated). You can type new values or select from suggestions.
  - **Custom Scenario** -- If you chose the **Scenario** type, describe the scenario.
  - **Intake Workflow** -- If you chose the **Intake** type, select the relevant workflow.
3. Click to confirm. The notification is saved and appears in the list.

---

## Managing Notifications

All your notifications appear in a table. Each row shows:

- **Type** -- Color-coded tag (blue for Call, green for Text, purple for Voicemail, etc.)
- **Method** -- Email or SMS
- **Recipients** -- The addresses or phone numbers receiving alerts
- **Status** -- Whether the notification is enabled

### Customizing a Notification

Click on a notification to open its detail view. From here you can:

- **Edit recipients** -- Add or remove email addresses and phone numbers
- **Toggle content sections** -- For call notifications, you can control what is included:
  * **Show Transcript** -- Include the call transcript
  * **Show Call Summary** -- Include the AI-generated summary
  * **Show Intake Forms** -- Include submitted intake form data
  * **Show Workflow** -- Include workflow results
  * **Show Call Summary Text** -- Include summary as text
  * **Show Call Info Link Text** -- Include a link to the full call details
- **Preview** -- See a sample of the email or SMS before saving

### Deleting a Notification

Click the delete icon on any notification row to remove it. If you remove all recipients from a notification, it is automatically deleted.

---

## Empty Call Notifications

You can toggle whether you receive notifications for empty or very short calls (e.g., a caller who hangs up immediately). This is controlled by a separate toggle on the notifications page.

---

## Previewing Notifications

Before saving, you can preview what your email or SMS notification will look like:

- **Preview Email** -- Opens a rendered preview of the notification email
- **Preview SMS** -- Shows the text message format

---

## Recipient Limits

Depending on your subscription plan, there may be a limit on the number of notification recipients you can add. The dashboard will notify you when you reach this limit.

---

## Next Steps

- Sent Notifications History -- View a log of all notifications that have been sent

# Sent Notifications History

The Sent Notifications log shows every notification email and SMS your AI receptionist has sent. Use it to verify that alerts are being delivered, troubleshoot delivery issues, and review past activity.

---

## Where to Find It

The Sent Notifications section is displayed at the bottom of the **Manage Notifications** page. Scroll down past your notification rules to reach the **Sent Notifications** heading.

---

## Viewing the Log

Notifications are displayed in a table with the following columns:

| Column      | Description                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Type**    | The event type, shown as a color-coded tag: Call (blue), Text (green), CRM (cyan), Intake (magenta), Scenario (orange), Voicemail (purple), Robocall (red), Calendar (pink) |
| **From**    | The sender address                                                                                                                                                          |
| **To**      | The recipient address                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Subject** | The notification subject line                                                                                                                                               |
| **Date**    | When the notification was sent                                                                                                                                              |
| **Status**  | Delivery status tag (see below)                                                                                                                                             |
| **Action**  | A **Preview** button to view the full notification content                                                                                                                  |

---

## Delivery Statuses

Each notification has one of these statuses:

| Status        | Meaning                                                      |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Queued**    | Waiting to be sent                                           |
| **Stored**    | Saved but not yet delivered                                  |
| **Accepted**  | Accepted by the email provider                               |
| **Delivered** | Successfully delivered to the recipient                      |
| **Opened**    | The recipient opened the email                               |
| **Failed**    | Delivery failed (hover over the info icon to see the reason) |

Failed or rejected notifications display a reason tooltip explaining what went wrong.

---

## Searching and Filtering

### Search

Use the **Search by recipient or subject...** field at the top to find specific notifications.

### Filters

Click the **Filters** button to reveal additional filter options:

- **Email Type** -- Filter by Call, Text, CRM, Intake, Scenario, Voicemail, Calendar, or Other
- **Status** -- Filter by Queued, Stored, Accepted, Delivered, Opened, or Failed
- **Date Range** -- Select a start and end date to narrow results

Filters can be combined. For example, filter for "Call" type with "Failed" status in the last 7 days to find undelivered call alerts.

---

## Previewing a Notification

Click **Preview** in the Action column of any row to open a detail drawer. The drawer shows:

- **Subject line** and **sender/recipient** at the top
- **Status** with a color-coded tag
- **Date** the notification was sent
- **Reason** (if the notification failed)
- **Tags** (if any)
- **Full content** -- The rendered HTML email body, or plain text if HTML is not available

Close the drawer by clicking the X or clicking outside it.

---

## Pagination

The table displays 10 notifications per page. Use the pagination controls at the bottom to navigate between pages.

# Integrations Overview

Frontdesk AI connects with 50+ third-party tools so your AI receptionist can sync data, trigger workflows, and automate tasks across your business stack. This guide covers the integrations available and how to find the right one for your needs.

---

## Browsing integrations

Visit the **Integrations** page to explore all available connections. The page opens with a hero section and a search bar where you can type a tool name (for example, "HubSpot" or "Slack") to filter results instantly.

### Category filters

Below the search bar you will see category buttons. Click any category to narrow the list:

- **All** -- every integration
- **Property Management** -- Buildium, AppFolio, Rentec Direct, Yardi, and more
- **CRM** -- HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Pipedrive, Close, Freshsales, and more
- **Scheduling** -- Google Calendar, Calendly, Cal.com, Acuity Scheduling, and more
- **Communication** -- Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Twilio, RingCentral, and more
- **Automation** -- Zapier, Make, GoHighLevel, n8n, Pabbly Connect, and more
- **Marketing** -- Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, Klaviyo, Constant Contact, and more
- **Other** -- additional integrations that don't fit the categories above

### Direction filters

You can also filter by data flow direction:

- **All Directions** -- show everything
- **Inbound (AI Receptionist)** -- integrations that push data from incoming calls into other tools
- **Outbound (AI Calls)** -- integrations designed for outbound AI calling campaigns

### Popular integrations

When no filters are active, a **Popular Integrations** section appears at the top highlighting:

- **Frontdesk + HubSpot** -- sync call data, contacts, and leads with HubSpot CRM automatically
- **Frontdesk + Zapier** -- connect to 5,000+ apps with automated Zaps
- **Frontdesk + Google Calendar** -- automatically book appointments on your Google Calendar from calls
- **Frontdesk + Salesforce** -- push call logs and lead data directly into Salesforce
- **Frontdesk + Slack** -- get real-time call notifications and summaries in Slack channels
- **Frontdesk + GoHighLevel** -- trigger GHL workflows from AI receptionist calls and texts

Click any integration card to open its detail page with setup steps and capabilities.

---

## Types of integrations in Frontdesk

Beyond the marketplace integrations above, Frontdesk offers several built-in integration features you can configure directly from your receptionist dashboard:

| Feature                     | What it does                                                          |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Zapier Integration**      | Provides an API key you paste into Zapier to connect with 5,000+ apps |
| **Google Calendar Sync**    | Two-way sync between Frontdesk scheduling and your Google Calendar    |
| **GoHighLevel Integration** | OAuth connection to push data into GHL workflows and calendars        |
| **Post-Call Webhook**       | Sends call summary data to any URL you specify after each call        |
| **API Workflows**           | Makes real-time API calls during live conversations                   |
| **Email / Gmail**           | Connects Gmail so the AI can read and respond to emails               |
| **API Workflow Templates**  | Pre-built templates organized by industry and CRM type                |

Each of these is covered in its own article in this section.

---

## Getting help

If you don't see the integration you need, click **Contact Sales** on the Integrations page. Frontdesk also provides a powerful API that works with virtually any tool -- the team can help you set up a custom connection.

# Zapier Integration

Connect your Frontdesk AI receptionist to 6,000+ apps through Zapier. Zapier lets you build automated workflows ("Zaps") that trigger when calls are received, appointments are booked, or leads are captured.

## Video walkthrough

https://www.youtube.com/embed/-L3dWjeBhjE

---

## Overview

The Zapier integration gives you three credentials you'll paste into Zapier:

- **Zapier Invite Link** -- a private link to access the Frontdesk integration inside Zapier
- **API Key** -- authenticates your Zapier connection
- **Username** -- identifies your Frontdesk account

A status badge shows whether the integration is **Enabled** or **Disabled**.

---

## Setting up Zapier

1. Open your receptionist dashboard and navigate to the **Advanced Settings** section.
2. Find the **Zapier Integration** card.
3. Copy the **Zapier Invite Link** and open it in your browser. This gives you access to the Frontdesk integration inside Zapier.
4. Copy the **API Key** by clicking the copy icon next to the field.
5. Copy the **Username** the same way.
6. In Zapier, create a new Zap and choose Frontdesk as the trigger or action app.
7. When Zapier prompts you for credentials, paste your **API Key** and **Username**.

For detailed step-by-step instructions with screenshots, click **Click Here for Instructions** below the credential fields. This links to a full tutorial on the Frontdesk website.

---

## What you can automate

Common Zaps include:

- **New call received** -- push call details to a Google Sheet, CRM, or Slack channel
- **Appointment booked** -- create a calendar event or send a confirmation email
- **Lead captured** -- add a new contact to your CRM or email marketing tool
- **Post-call summary** -- send transcripts and call summaries to a project management tool

---

## Tips

- Each receptionist (agent) has its own Zapier credentials. Make sure you select the correct agent before copying your keys.
- If you update your agent or create a new one, you may need to reconnect in Zapier.
- Test your Zap with a sample call to confirm data flows correctly before going live.

# Google Calendar Integration

Sync your Google Calendar with Frontdesk so your AI receptionist knows your real-time availability and can book appointments directly onto your calendar during phone calls.

## Prerequisites

- A Frontdesk AI account with an active receptionist
- A Google account with at least one writable Google Calendar

## How it works

Once connected, the integration works in two directions:

- **Google Calendar to Frontdesk** — all existing events in your Google Calendar are blocked off so the AI receptionist will not double-book those slots.
- **Frontdesk to Google Calendar** — any appointments booked through calls are synced back to your Google Calendar automatically.

## Connecting your Google Calendar

1. Open your receptionist dashboard and navigate to the scheduling or calendar section.
2. Look for the **Google Calendar Sync** card, labeled **Highly Recommended**.
3. Click the **Connect** button (it shows the Google icon).
4. A Google sign-in window will open. Sign in and grant Frontdesk access to your calendar.
5. After authorization, a **Select Calendar** modal appears. It lists all Google Calendars you have owner or writer access to. Your primary calendar is pre-selected.
6. Choose the calendar you want to sync and click **Connect**.

You will see a success message: "Calendar connected successfully — Pulling in all existing events from your calendar. This may take a few minutes."

## Managing your connected calendar

Once connected, the card updates to show:

- **Google Calendar Sync** — with a "Connected to [calendar name]" label
- A **Refresh** button (reload icon) to manually re-sync
- A **Disconnect** button to remove the connection

### Prevent double bookings

Below the connection info, you will see a **Prevent double bookings** toggle with the description "Block slots with existing Google Calendar events."

- **On (recommended)** — the AI will not book over time slots that already have events on your Google Calendar.
- **Off** — the AI may book appointments even when there is a conflict. A warning dialog will confirm: "Frontdesk may book over slots that already have events on your Google Calendar."

## Disconnecting

1. Click the red **Disconnect** button on the connected calendar card.
2. Confirm in the dialog by clicking **Disconnect**.

This removes the calendar sync. Events already created will remain on your Google Calendar.

## Troubleshooting

- **No calendars found** — make sure your Google account has at least one calendar where you are an owner or writer. Shared read-only calendars will not appear.
- **Sync is slow** — initial sync can take a few minutes to pull in all existing events. Use the refresh button to check progress.
- **Connection lost** — if the card shows "Setting up connection," the OAuth handshake may still be in progress. Wait a moment and refresh the page.

# Custom Webhooks

Send post-call data to any URL after your AI receptionist finishes a call. Use webhooks to push call summaries, caller details, and other data to your own systems or third-party tools.

## Video walkthrough

https://www.youtube.com/embed/4h-rjvchGKc

## Prerequisites

- A Frontdesk AI account with an active receptionist
- A server or service that can receive HTTP requests at a publicly accessible URL

## How it works

After every call, Frontdesk sends an HTTP request to the endpoint you configure. The request contains structured data about the call, including the caller's information, call summary, and any data collected during the conversation.

## Adding a webhook

1. Open your receptionist dashboard and navigate to the **Overview** page.
2. Scroll to the **Post-Call Webhook** section.
3. Click the **Add** button to open the webhook form.

Fill in the following fields:

- **Method** — choose the HTTP method for the request: **POST**, **PUT**, or **PATCH**
- **Endpoint** — enter the full URL where Frontdesk should send the data (e.g., `https://example.com/webhook`)

The endpoint must be a valid URL. Click **Save** to activate your webhook.

## Viewing your webhook

Once saved, the webhook card displays:

- **Method** — the HTTP method you selected
- **Endpoint** — the URL receiving the data

## Editing a webhook

1. Click the **Edit** button on the webhook card.
2. Update the **Method** or **Endpoint** as needed.
3. Save your changes.

## Deleting a webhook

1. Click the **Delete** button on the webhook card.
2. Confirm the deletion when prompted.

A success message confirms: "Webhook deleted successfully!"

## Use cases

- Push call data to a CRM that is not natively supported
- Log calls in a custom database or spreadsheet
- Trigger internal workflows in tools like n8n, Make, or your own backend
- Feed call summaries into a reporting dashboard

## Troubleshooting

- **Invalid endpoint URL** — make sure the URL starts with `https://` and is publicly accessible.
- **No data received** — verify your server is listening on the correct path and returns a 200-level status code. Check your server logs for incoming requests.
- **Webhook not firing** — ensure the webhook is active (visible on the card). If you recently added it, try making a test call to trigger the delivery.

# API Workflows

API Workflows let your AI receptionist make real-time API calls during a live conversation. When a caller asks about something that requires a data lookup -- like pricing, order status, or appointment availability -- the AI can fetch that information from your systems on the spot and relay it to the caller.

## Video walkthrough

https://www.youtube.com/embed/HhRlhxqprtw

## Prerequisites

- A Frontdesk AI account with an active receptionist
- An API endpoint your receptionist should call (your own backend, a third-party API, etc.)

## How it works

You define a workflow with:

1. **A scenario** -- the situation that triggers the API call (e.g., "Whenever the caller asks anything about the MacBook")
2. **An API endpoint** -- the URL, method, headers, and body
3. **Response mapping** -- which parts of the API response to extract and what to tell the caller

When the AI detects that a caller's request matches your scenario, it fires the API call, extracts the data you specified, and uses it in the conversation.

## Creating an API workflow

1. Open your receptionist dashboard and navigate to the **Overview** page.
2. Scroll to the **API Workflows** section.
3. Click **Add** to open the workflow form.

### Workflow fields

- **Name** -- a descriptive label for the workflow (e.g., "Get MacBook Details")
- **Scenario** -- describe when this workflow should trigger. Write this in plain language (e.g., "Trigger this action whenever the caller asks anything about the MacBook.")
- **URL** -- the full API endpoint URL
- **Method** -- **GET**, **POST**, **PUT**, or **DELETE**
- **Headers** -- key-value pairs such as `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` and `Content-Type: application/json`
- **Body** -- the request body (for POST/PUT requests)
- **Response Data** -- map JSON paths from the response to variable names and prompts that tell the AI how to use the data

### Caller information extraction

You can configure the workflow to extract information from the caller during the conversation:

- **Extracted Call Info** -- specific fields to collect from the caller (e.g., hard disk size, core preference), each with a name, type, and description
- **Extract from Context** -- information to infer from the conversation history (e.g., whether the caller is an existing customer)

### Additional options

- **Speech to Emit** -- what the AI says while the API call is in progress (e.g., "Fetching MacBook details. Please hold on for a moment.")
- **Timeout** -- how many seconds to wait before giving up on the API call
- **Repeatable** -- whether the workflow can be triggered multiple times in a single call

## Workflow types

Frontdesk supports two workflow types:

- **Scenario-based** -- triggers when the caller's request matches a specific scenario
- **Knowledge Base Loader** -- fetches data from an API and loads it into the AI's context as additional knowledge

## Using pre-built templates

Instead of building a workflow from scratch, you can start from a template.

1. Navigate to the **API Workflow Templates** page from your receptionist dashboard.
2. Browse templates by category using the tabs at the top: **CRM**, **Auto Repair**, **Beauty**, **Construction**, **Fitness**, **Food**, **HVAC**, **Legal**, **Real Estate**, **Retail**, **Technology**, and more.
3. Use the search bar to find templates by name.
4. Click a template card to preview it, then apply it to your receptionist.

If you need an integration that is not listed, click the request integration option to submit a request to the Frontdesk team.

## Managing workflows

Each saved workflow appears as a card in the API Workflows section showing:

- The workflow name and scenario
- An **Edit** button to modify the configuration
- A **Delete** button to remove it
- An **Expand/Collapse** toggle to view details
- A **Duplicate** button to copy the workflow
- An **Error Logs** button to view any recent failures
- An enable/disable toggle to activate or deactivate the workflow

## Workflow availability

You can configure when a workflow is active using the availability settings, restricting it to specific days and hours if needed.

## Troubleshooting

- **API call timing out** -- increase the timeout value or check that your API endpoint responds within the configured window.
- **Incorrect data returned** -- verify that your JSON path expressions match the actual response structure. Test the API endpoint independently first.
- **Workflow not triggering** -- make sure the scenario description clearly matches what callers are likely to say. The more specific the scenario, the more reliably the AI will activate it.
- **Error logs** -- click the error logs icon on a workflow card to see recent failures and diagnose issues.

# Email / Gmail Integration

Connect your Gmail account to Frontdesk AI so your receptionist can read, draft, and send emails on your behalf. This turns your AI receptionist into an email assistant that can monitor your inbox and respond automatically.

## Prerequisites

- A Frontdesk AI account
- A Google account with Gmail

## Connecting Gmail

1. Open your receptionist dashboard.
2. Navigate to the **Email** page (look for the mail icon in the sidebar).
3. On the **Connection** tab, you will see the **Google (Gmail) account** card.
4. Click the **Connect Google account** button.
5. A Google sign-in window opens. Sign in and grant Frontdesk permission to send, read, and modify emails on your behalf.
6. Once authorized, the card updates to show **Connected** with your email address.

Your tokens are stored securely and used only for this feature.

## Enabling email monitoring

After connecting Gmail, an **Incoming email monitoring** card appears:

1. Toggle the switch to **on**.
2. When enabled, your AI receptionist will automatically read and respond to incoming emails in real time.
3. A green label confirms: "Active -- monitoring your inbox for new emails."

Toggle it off at any time to stop automatic monitoring.

## Email Agent tabs

Once connected (and with the email configuration feature enabled), the Email page shows several tabs: **Overview**, **AI & Preferences**, **Labels**, **Tickets**, **Forwarding**, **Campaign Templates**, and **Connection**. The Overview tab summarizes activity such as emails processed and drafts created.

## AI & Preferences tab

Configure how your AI handles emails from the **AI & Preferences** tab:

- **Drafting Instructions** -- customize how the AI drafts email replies on your behalf (e.g., "Always greet the customer by name. Never offer discounts without manager approval.")
- **Labeling Instructions** -- guide how the AI categorizes and labels emails (e.g., "Mark any email mentioning refunds as 'Urgent'.")
- **CRM Lead Creation Prompt** -- customize how the AI qualifies and creates new CRM leads from incoming emails
- **CRM Settings** -- toggle **Create leads from emails** (automatically add qualifying senders to your CRM) and **CRM lead email notifications** (get notified when a lead emails you)
- **Scheduling Notifications** -- toggle meeting request notifications, which include an "Add to Google Calendar" link when a lead asks to schedule a meeting
- **Email Signature** -- appended to all outgoing emails; provide both a **Plain Text** and an **HTML** version (the HTML editor includes a live preview)

Click **Save All Preferences** at the bottom to apply your changes.

## Labels tab

The **Labels** tab manages the labels your AI uses to classify incoming email:

- Labels are grouped into **Predefined Labels**, **Configured Labels** (custom labels with a description), and **Unconfigured Labels** (custom labels without one)
- **Create Label** -- add a new label with a name, color, and a description of when it should be applied. The description is required for AI email classification
- **Edit** label descriptions to help the AI understand when to use each label
- **Delete** labels you no longer need
- Toggle label **visibility**

If you see an **Additional permissions required** banner, Gmail label management needs updated permissions. Click **Reconnect Gmail** to re-authorize; your existing email connection is preserved.

## Tickets tab

The **Tickets** tab creates support tickets from incoming email automatically:

- **Escalation scenarios** -- click **Add scenario**, give it a title (e.g., "Refund request"), and describe when it should trigger a ticket (e.g., "Customer mentions they want a refund or expresses dissatisfaction with a purchase"). The AI checks every incoming email against your enabled scenarios and opens a ticket on a match. Each scenario has an on/off switch.
- **Label-based tickets** -- check any of your configured labels to automatically create a ticket whenever an incoming email is classified with one of them.

Changes on this tab save automatically; a "Saving… / Saved" indicator appears at the top right.

## Forwarding tab

The **Forwarding** tab auto-forwards matching emails to another address:

1. Click **Add rule**.
2. Enter a **Rule name** (e.g., "Urgent billing").
3. Describe the **Forwarding condition** -- when the rule should trigger (e.g., "emails about billing issues, unpaid invoices, or payment failures").
4. Enter the **Forward to** email address.
5. Leave **Enabled** on and click **Add**.

When an incoming email matches a rule's condition, it is forwarded to the specified address automatically. Toggle rules on and off with the switch, click a rule's name to edit it, or use the delete button to remove it. Changes save automatically.

## Campaign Templates tab

The **Campaign Templates** tab holds reusable email templates for your sequences and campaigns:

1. Click **Create Template**.
2. Give the template a subject and build the body from blocks: text, image, button, divider, and raw HTML. Drag blocks to reorder, and duplicate or remove them as needed.
3. Preview the result (including a mobile preview) before saving.

Existing templates can be edited, previewed, or deleted from the list.

## Disconnecting Gmail

1. Go to the **Email** page, **Connection** tab.
2. Click the **Disconnect Gmail** button next to the connected account.
3. The connection is removed. Emails already sent or received are not affected.

## Troubleshooting

- **OAuth window does not open** -- check your browser popup blocker settings and allow popups for the Frontdesk dashboard.
- **Monitoring not activating** -- if toggling the switch shows an error, the AI may need additional Gmail permissions. Reconnect your Google account to grant full access.
- **Labels tab missing** -- the labels feature requires the email configuration feature flag to be enabled. Contact support if you do not see this tab.
